title: Roadmap Roundup - June 4, 2025
summary: 06/04/2025 - 6:00 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!
body_html:
06/04/2025 - 6:00 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!

Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.

Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.

Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.

With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!

-CIG Community Team

Notable Changes: June 4, 2025

Release View

4.2.0

Irradiated Apex Valakkar

Adding the irradiated Apex Valakkar that players can find near the Research Facility while doing the Storm Breaker sandbox activity. This was previously listed under the "New Creatures" card.

The card has been set to Committed.

Irradiated Adult Valakkar

Adding the irradiated Adult Valakkar that players can find near the Research Facility while doing the Storm Breaker sandbox activity. This was previously listed under the "New Creatures" card.

The card has been set to Committed.

Irradiated Juvenile Valakkar

Adding the irradiated Juvenile Valakkar that players can find near the Research Facility while doing the Storm Breaker sandbox activity. This was previously listed under the "New Creatures" card.

The card has been set to Committed.

Irradiated Kopion

Adding the irradiated Kopion that players can find roaming near the Research Facility while doing the Storm Breaker sandbox activity. This was previously listed under the "New Creatures" card. These hostile beasts hunt in packs!

The card has been set to Committed.

New Hairstyles (4.2.0)

Adding four additional hairstyles.

The card has been set to Committed.

Radiation

Implementing dangerous radiation zones in specific locations, forcing players to adapt with specialized gear and strategic navigation.

The card has been set to Committed.

ASD Research Facility

Strategically located on Pyro I, Associated Science and Development facilities that provided essential infrastructure and sandbox gameplay opportunities for planetary operations.

The card has been set to Committed.

ASD Datacenter

Strategically placed on Pyro IV, Associated Science and Development datacenters are providing key infrastructure and sandbox gameplay opportunities for planetary operations.

The card has been set to Committed.

Storm Breaker Sandbox Activity

Adding the Storm Breaker Sandbox activity, utilizing new gameplay mechanics to tell new stories in the 'verse.

The card has been set to Committed.

ARGO ATLS IKTI

Adding the ATLS IKTI, and ATLS GEO IKTI: versatile new combat suits developed for upcoming challenges, ready to prove their value in an upcoming new Sandbox Activity. They both are equipped with dual weapons, and the GEO IKTI version keeps its backpack for a jumping ability with adjusted gear slots to fit FPS weapons and gadgets.

The card has been set to Committed.

Wikelo Special Ships (4.2.0)

Adding multiple new ships and vehicles to the ever-expanding Wikelo's Emporium: Mirai Guardian QI, Anvil Mk2 Super Hornet, MISC Fortune, Aopoa Nox, Mirai Pulse, RSI Ursa Medivac. These ships and vehicles can be unlocked by bringing the NPC Wikelo a number of favors in exchange for rewards.

The card has been set to Committed.

VOLT Laser Shotgun "Prism"

Adding a cutting-edge energy shotgun that ramps up its pellet spread with heat, delivering brutal close-range bursts powered by VOLT.

The card has been set to Committed.

Sterling Exploration Suit

Introducing the Sterling Exploration Suit: a heavy utility armor built to withstand extreme radiation, enabling safe traversal through the most hazardous zones.

The card has been set to Committed.

Dynamic Rain

Adding dynamic rain in specific locations, as a first step toward Genesis: Dynamic Weather.

The card has been set to Committed.

Aegis Idris-P

Adding the Idris Peacekeeper. A ship that secured our past and continues to define our future, this steadfast, tactical, civilian class incarnation of the UEEN darling is available to fly for the first time.

The card has been set to Released.

Greycat MTC

Adding the MTC vehicle, Greycat's comprehensive suit and gun storage, defensive weaponry, and its customary off-road ability.

The card has been set to Released.

Mirai Guardian MX

Adding the Mirai Guardian MX. Keeping the cutting-edge design of its predecessor, the MX refines destruction to a powerful art. Enhanced weaponry and shields mean Mirai, once again, has put you ahead of every other single pilot flying.

The card has been set to Released.

MISC Starlancer TAC

Adding the Starlancer TAC ship, designed for tactical assault and rescue.

The card has been set to Released.

Anvil Asgard

Introducing Anvil’s new savior of the battlefield, the Asgard - a heavily armored vehicle-dropship equipped for boundless resilience in the hottest combat zones.

The card has been set to Released.

Join the discussion on Spectrum.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: 05/26/2025 - 8:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Happy Monday, everyone!
body_html:
05/26/2025 - 8:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Happy Monday, everyone!

There’s still time to swing by the Bevic Convention Center and take a few ships for a spin before Invictus Launch Week draws to a close. Whether you’re jumping in for the first time or taking another lap, now’s the perfect moment to enjoy the Free Fly and test some of the ‘verse’s best military-inspired ships before it ends on May 27. We’ve also really enjoyed seeing you share your experiences of the big event on the Community Hub, so keep those coming!

After Invictus Launch Week wraps up, we’ll begin rolling out ship naming waves for the Aegis Idris, starting with original concept owners and Golden Ticket holders. If that’s you, you can find the details in this Spectrum post. More waves will follow soon after.

Meanwhile, work continues on Alpha 4.2, with our teams iterating on early feedback from the Evocati. This update will include dynamic rain, improved kiosk interactions, new hairstyles, and more — and we're aiming to open up for broader testing soon.

Lastly, the Bar Citizen World Tour continues! This Saturday, May 31, we visit the heart of one of Europe's most vibrant cities: Lyon, France. If you're in the area, come meet the team, raise a glass, and celebrate all things Star Citizen with fellow enthusiasts. Check out our World Tour comm-link for more details on this event (and other upcoming ones).

Now, let's see what's going on this week

This Tuesday, keep an eye out for the May Squadron 42 Newsletter, because the ships of Squadron 42 are ready for their close-up! Make sure you're subscribed so you don't miss a frame.

Friday, you'll find a copy of the weekly RSI Newsletter delivered straight to your inbox.

On Saturday, it's time for the System 7 Finals by ATMO esports! After weeks of blistering speed, tight turns, and challenging race tracks, the best of the best are set to battle it out for glory. Tune in to ATMO esports' channel from 6 pm UTC to see who will emerge victorious.

Fly low, and fly fast!

body_html:
May Newsletter BEHIND THE BADGE

Although much is known of the accolades of our proud 42nd Squadron, inside intel of these history-making achievements has been for military eyes only - until now. The 42nd Squadron made their mark during the Battle for Centauri, a standoff which ultimately concluded the second Tevarin war, when, under the leadership of Captain Alexandra Dunlevy, they feigned retreat in order to form an ambush of the Tevarin fleet.

This tactical maneuver undoubtedly led to the UEEN’s victory and is still studied by new recruits and military personnel to this day. Join us, as Invictus 2955 comes to an end, in celebrating not only our serving fleet, but also commemorating the ships, crew and lives of some of the UEEN’s finest, the 42nd Squadron.

Building off a career that's sprawled over thirty years, Declan's worked on every fighter in the fleet to become a walking encyclopedia of parts, weapons, engines, and armor. As more and more mechanics turned to him for his expansive knowledge, he grew into a natural position of authority, eventually earning Chief Petty Officer and assuming the celebrated role of Krugeri Pit Chief. He may love nothing more than the thrum of a busy flight deck, but will always make time for his crew and flight officers alike to talk about the simple joys of flying.

title: Roadmap Roundup - May 21, 2025
summary: 05/21/2025 - 9:00 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!
body_html:
05/21/2025 - 9:00 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!

Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.

Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.

Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.

Note: REDACTED cards are purposefully hiding details, to avoid spoiling content for players. As we have now started our test cycle with the Evocati, you will learn more as we progress through the development of 4.2.0 and beyond.

With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!

-CIG Community Team

Notable Changes: May 21, 2025

Release View

4.1

Missions - Local Site Maintenance

Implementing new missions into the persistent universe, first appearing in Pyro's outposts. Players will be tasked with going to the location and fixing equipment with fuses and repairing pipes (RMC Repair) with your multi-tool.

The card has been set to Released.

Missions - Animal Population Control

Enabling animal population control Missions.

The card has been set to Released.

Mission - Hunt The Polaris

Adding a new Fleet Week mission. A Polaris has been stolen by the Frontier Fighters, and the CDF is tasked by the UEE Navy to hunt it through the Stanton system, isolate it, and kill it. The mission will be offered rarely, can be shared, and will only have one active at a time. Once completed, a reward will be given.

The card has been set to Released.

New Hairstyles (4.1.1)

Adding four additional hairstyles with Update 4.1.1.

The card has been set to Released.

VOLT SMG "Quartz"

Adding a compact, yet devastating firearm designed for those who need maximum firepower in a minimal frame.

The card has been set to Released.

Components Balance Pass

Balancing ship components and shield generators based on their class types.

The card has been set to Released.

Wikelo Special Ships (4.1.1)

Adding the following Special Ships to Wikelo's Emporium: MISC Starlancer MAX, Aegis Sabre Firebird, Aegis Sabre Peregrine, RSI Zeus ES, RSI Zeus CL, Crusader Intrepid, with top-grade components (Currently Stock modules. It will be fixed in 4.2.0). These ships can be unlocked by bringing the NPC Wikelo a number of favors in exchange of rewards.

The card has been set to Released.

Space Combat Missions: UEE Training, Patrol, Ambush

Adding new missions to the 'verse.

These cards have been set to Released.

New column, 4.2.0

New Creatures

Adding multiple new creatures to the 'verse.

The card has been set to Tentative.

New Hairstyles (4.2.0)

Adding four additional hairstyles with Update 4.2.0

The card has been set to Tentative.

Radiation

Implementing dangerous radiation zones in specific locations, forcing players to adapt with specialized gear and strategic navigation.

The card has been set to Tentative.

ASD Research Facility

Strategically located on Pyro I, Associated Science and Development facilities that provided essential infrastructure and sandbox gameplay opportunities for planetary operations.

The card has been set to Tentative.

ASD Datacenter

Strategically placed on Pyro IV, Associated Science and Development datacenters are providing key infrastructure and sandbox gameplay opportunities for planetary operations.

The card has been set to Tentative.

Sandbox Activity

Adding a Sandbox activity utilizing new gameplay mechanics, and vehicles to tell new stories in the 'verse.

The card has been set to Tentative.

ARGO ATLS IKTI

Adding the ARGO ATLS IKTI is a versatile new combat vehicle developed for upcoming challenges, ready to prove its value in an upcoming new Sandbox Activity.

The card has been set to Tentative.

Wikelo Special Ships (4.2.0)

Adding multiple new ships and vehicles to the ever-expanding Wikelo's Emporium. These ships and vehicles can be unlocked by bringing the NPC Wikelo a number of favors in exchange for rewards.

The card has been set to Tentative.

VOLT Laser Shotgun "Prism"

Adding a cutting-edge energy shotgun that ramps up its pellet spread with heat, delivering brutal close-range bursts powered by VOLT.

The card has been set to Tentative.

Sterling Exploration Suit

Introducing the Sterling Exploration Suit: a heavy utility armor built to withstand extreme radiation, enabling safe traversal through the most hazardous zones.

The card has been set to Tentative.

Dynamic Rain

Adding dynamic rain in specific locations, as a first step toward Genesis: Dynamic Weather.

The card has been set to Tentative.

New Global Event (4.2.x)

Adding a global, cross-shard event that builds on collaboration and competition. Scheduled to come in a 4.2.x patch.

The card has been set to Tentative.

New Space Combat Mission - Defend (4.2.x)

Adding a collection of missions tasking citizens to defend various places against attackers. Scheduled to come in a 4.2.x patch.

The card has been set to Tentative.

New Medium Utility armor (4.2.x)

Adding a new legendary Medium Utility armor. Scheduled to come in a 4.2.x patch.

The card has been set to Tentative.

Progress Tracker

We've made a few additions to the Progress Tracker, which you can review below. Just a reminder: when progress on a deliverable is marked as complete, it doesn’t necessarily mean it’s ready for release. It may still require downstream support, transition to another team for further work, or other additional steps before completion.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: 05/19/2025 - 10:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Happy Monday, everyone!
body_html:
05/19/2025 - 10:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Happy Monday, everyone!

Invictus Launch Week 2955 has officially touched down at Bevic Convention Center on ArcCorp! This annual event honors the legacy of the UEE Navy while giving everyone the chance to experience the ships and technology that defend the Empire. Don't miss the chance to test fly the best military-inspired ships with our Free Fly event, running from now through May 27. Plus, there are activities galore for pilots from all walks of life, offering something for everyone throughout Invictus Launch Week.

This year brings a special highlight - the Aegis Idris. Not only is it available to tour at the Aegis Idris Experience, but we’re also pleased to see this iconic capital ship take its place in the hangars and skies of the ‘verse, letting owners command one of the Navy’s most formidable vessels. To help you make the most of your time at Invictus, we've prepared a detailed FAQ covering everything you need to know about the big event (including Free Fly access, ship rentals, and more), and the Manufacturer Schedule to help you plan your test flights. As always, we look forward to seeing you share your favorite moments, ship impressions, and screenshots on the Community Hub, whether this is your first event or if you're an Invictus veteran.

Last Saturday, CON42 lit up the Bar Citizen World Tour with nearly 600 attendees coming together near Frankfurt for a weekend full of Star Citizen excitement. From incredible fan-built ship models to hands-on activities and thoughtful conversations, the event was packed with energy and shared passion. A massive thanks to the amazing organizers and everyone who joined us; it was one for the books! Next up: Lyon, France on May 31. More details on upcoming events here.

And finally, the team is full steam ahead as we prepare to release Alpha 4.2.0 to our Evocati testers this week — potentially as early as tonight! We’ll keep you posted as things progress, and we can’t wait for you to experience the new content coming your way soon.

Now, let's see what's going on this week

On Monday, Behind the Ships kicks off the week with a closer look at another ship making its debut this Invictus Launch Week - the Mirai Guardian MX, a heavy-hitting variant of the Guardian built to bring more bite to the fight. We'll also be publishing the Mirai Guardian MX Q&A.

This Tuesday, our servers will be offline for approximately 4 hours starting from 13:00 UTC / 8:00 AM CDT to accommodate essential infrastructure tuning on our backend systems and the implementation of stability upgrades. During this maintenance window, all gameplay systems will be unavailable; you will not be able to access the game until maintenance is complete. We will provide updates on the RSI Status Page as the maintenance progresses. Thanks for your patience as we carry out this work. We'll have the 'verse back up and running as soon as possible!

Wednesday will have the latest Roadmap Update alongside an explanatory Roadmap Roundup.

Friday, we close out with another Behind the Ships episode, this time featuring the Anvil Asgard, which will be accompanied by a Q&A Comm-Link. You'll also find a copy of the weekly RSI Newsletter delivered straight to your inbox.

This Saturday, Race 6, the last race before the System 7 finals, touches down in the tropical chaos of "Bermuda Bay", a track ATMO esports has cooked up featuring a brutal blend of speed and precision. Watch the 'verse's best pilots thread razor-thin island gaps and blast through breakneck straights in their Aopoa Noxes live on the ATMO esports' channel from 7 pm UTC.

Fly low, and fly fast!

title: Q&A: Anvil Asgard
summary: Q&A Asgard by Anvil Introducing Anvil’s new savior of the battlefield, the Asgard - a heavily armored vehicle equipped for boundless resilience in the hottest combat zones.
body_html:
Q&A Asgard by Anvil Introducing Anvil’s new savior of the battlefield, the Asgard - a heavily armored vehicle equipped for boundless resilience in the hottest combat zones.

We asked the Vehicle and Gameplay teams a few questions about Anvil's new dropship. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

What is the key difference between the Valkyrie and the Asgard? In what situations might a player choose one over the other? The primary difference is that the Asgard chassis has been extended to accommodate the on-board storage of a single Nova-tank-sized vehicle or one of the Anvil Atlas chassis family (Ballista, Spartan, and Centurion).

However, this is at the expense of crew accommodation and drop seats, which the Valkyrie houses. The crew requirement for the Asgard is lower than the Valkyrie, as some weapons are slaved to the pilot, allowing for significant forward-facing firepower. In comparison, the Valkyrie’s turrets provide greater coverage in all arcs beyond the front.

How many people can be accommodated in the Asgard dropship? How many when a Nova Tank is loaded? There are no dedicated drop seats in the Asgard. The crew requirement is only two players, these being a pilot and a second player either operating the manual lower turret or completing engineering-related work.

If the Asgard pilot is alone and without a gunner, how many forward-facing weapons can they operate? The pilot can control the six facing-forward S3 weapons along with the top-mounted missile rack.

Are the 2x S4 manual gunner turrets able to fire in an arc, or are they fixed to face forward? The manual gunner turrets can rotate 360 degrees with good downward-facing angles, allowing players to engage ground targets ahead of dropping vehicles into the area.

The Asgard has a significant amount of facing-forward weaponry, rather than multiple turrets covering all angles of defense as found on other dropships. What was the reasoning behind this design choice? We wanted there to be gameplay differences between the Asgard and other dropships, like the Valkyrie. It was a conscious design decision to provide most of the firepower as forward-facing to distinguish the Asgard amongst those other ships.

What was the reasoning behind equipping the Asgard with 16x S3 missiles? What threats or targets is it specifically designed to counter? The missiles were added to provide some ability to tackle threats outside of the front arc. However, missile lock is only possible from the pilot’s view, requiring players to keep targets in sight prior to launch.

Can you provide examples of missions, roles, or scenarios that the Asgard is intended for? The Asgard excels in missions that require transporting ground vehicles and cargo, either together or independently. With its large rear ramp, loading and unloading cargo is simple.

Does the Asgard feature a cargo grid in addition to its 180 SCU storage? Could this be used to transport ammo, fuel, and other equipment to the battlefield? The 180 SCU cargo grid is the only cargo grid on the vehicle and occupies the same area as the vehicle storage. This means that when a vehicle is aboard, cargo capacity is reduced.

Does the Asgard retain the lateral doors from its sister ship, the Valkyrie? Yes, along with the side door guns.

Does the pilot have good visibility beneath them to aid in landing troops? Is there an MFD landing camera system? We are still working on updated landing systems that utilize the radar displays to show the location of the ship relative to its surrounding terrain.

Can the four thrusters on the Asgard transition to VTOL mode? Yes, they can.

Is it possible to apply Valkyrie paints to the Asgard? No, the Asgard is treated as a new and separate vehicle, so paints from the Valkyrie are not applicable to the Asgard.

DISCLAIMER These answers accurately reflect development's intentions at the time of writing, but the company and development team reserve the right to adapt, improve, or change feature and ship designs in response to feedback, playtesting, design revisions, or other considerations to improve balance or the quality of the game overall.

title: Re: Multi-View implementation? (Multiple Monitor Display)
summary: This thread reminds me of an old technique that seems to have been lost to time. Back in the olden days, the original Doom supported multi-monitors using 3 separate cameras. Actually that's misleading. It used 3 separate computers (or more). You'd launch the game with networking using one machine as the host then when launching the other clients, you could specify a view rotational offset. So you'd have a screen looking forward, one looking 90 degrees to the right and another lookin 90 degrees to the left.  I loved that silly hack! :grin:

summary: I should point out that this isn't my photo. I had to throw away most of my game boxes a number of years ago because I ran out of space. The only ones I still have are for Elite, X-Wing, Wing Commander: Prophesy, and Flight Unlimited (and I've only now realised the pattern).  I guess Flight Unlimited is the odd-one-out, because it's not space-based. It was a great game though. It was a DOS game from 1995 that had an amazing flight model based on "real-time computational fluid dynamics." It felt so realistic to fly, including stresses on the airframe that could cause your plane to break up if manoeuvring too aggressively. It's a bit of a treasure, because apparently the flight model was incredibly hard to understand, so when the programmer responsible was fired after the first game, they couldn't understand it well enough to integrate into the sequels.

title: Re: Multi-View implementation? (Multiple Monitor Display)
summary: A few years back nvidia introduced a feature called SMP (Simultaneous Multi-Projection). That was a hardware solution to allow you to render multiple views without having to repeat lots of calculations (culling geometry outside of the view frustum for example). It wasn't something easy to just turn on, you have to put effort into using it, and this being back in 2015 or so, few people used tripple screens, so it was rarely implemented. Last I heard it didn't get much use outside of VR.  I'm not sure if there are modern alternatives.

title: Re: Multi-View implementation? (Multiple Monitor Display)
summary: What you're describing makes me think of this pretty cool demo someone made by reversing a Wii remote and sensor bar (where moving your head works): https://youtu.be/Jd3-eiid-Uw?si=paL-OnEpavNTK4jZ&t=116 I could see that having some pretty cool effects with multiple screens.   That also fits well for optimisations like Foveated Rendering too. That's where you reduce the rendering complexity of areas in your peripheral vision. Your fovea is the very central part of your retina where you have a very dense collection of cells able to make out details. Humans have a surprisingly wide field of view (about 220°), but you can only make out details over a very small portion of that area from your foveal view and surrounding areas, creating your "macular vision". This is approximately 6° wide. So if you can render everything outside of that range with a more simplistic model you can make some great savings. Of course it then raises other challenges: it doesn't work if  you're livestreaming, your eye tracking needs to be up to speed, you need to make sure the objects in the peripheral view don't 'pop' or look inconsistent, because you peripheral vision is excellent at detecting motion, etc. But it's an interesting concept.

title: Re: IFCS info from SPViewer
summary: These are just scaling numbers that we use to affect the flight handling. E.g. when thrusters are placed far from the center of mass of a ship, you do not need a lot of thrust to create torque as opposed to linear movement. So the modifiers help us balance things out. We can also use them for very quick tuning passes without rebalancing the whole flight tunung for a ship.  However when these numbers change, it does not necessarily mean that a ship performs better or worse. They can also be just corrective measures to compensate e.g. increases in ship mass, etc. So in short, these are not player facing values and you cannot infer from them if anything has actually changed.

title: Re: IFCS info from SPViewer
summary: I understand the argument, but specifically for flight a lot of these numbers might not help you make a good decision, the dynamics are often too complex. Easy public facing numbers on the FM right now are things like top speed or so but with NFM that will change. Because the FM will become dynamic as changes in mass will not just affect the accelerations but also top speeds. We couldn't show you a lot of data on a ship that is powered off, literally all of the values are dynamically available only when a ship is fully powered and the physics calculate how heavy that ship is (as our thrusters actually produce thrust which in turn defines the available accelerations / Gs defined by the mass). You throw in heavier shield generator into the loadout, it will change your acceleration and top speeds.  We actually had discussion several times what to show ... some of the flight data is really hard to show in an offline manner so to speak. Personally I also don't think that every number needs to be public as min maxing can easily hide things or choices. There is a good example from WWII on the performance of FW190 vs the BF109. In raw performance the FW190 was advantageous in almost all categories, climb rate, speed, etc. ... but pilots often preferred the BF109 and the reason wasn't easily put in objective numbers ... it was much more pleasant to fly ... so picking the better plane is actually a subjetive feeling of the pilot. Some of these principles can be applied to SC's flight model in certain areas ... so we still have some discussions to do in that regard.

title: Re: IFCS info from SPViewer
summary: We do have concepts somewhere for a more technical flight info page (similar to those flight diagnostics pages that you find in RL aircraft) that lists things like current / mag Gs, velocities in every direction, current weight, acceleration against gravity (so it can show you if you can actually hover, take off or savely land), etc. We know all that information already and it's not hard to put it on some MFD ... but that also needs to be designed first and implemented and compared to other things it's more a side thing to do when bigger things are out of the way. It's not hard but it's more polish for NFM than priority work if that makes sense.

title: Re: Does Star Citizen have occlusion culling?
summary: Yes, we have occlusion culling. Currently CPU-side, which makes it easier to do things like prevent shadow calculations from even being submitted, though this has the downside that it can sometimes get holes in it when moving quickly.
body_html: Yes, we have occlusion culling. Currently CPU-side, which makes it easier to do things like prevent shadow calculations from even being submitted, though this has the downside that it can sometimes get holes in it when moving quickly.

title: IAE 2955 FAQ - Orison Welcomes You!
summary: The Intergalactic Aerospace Expo (IAE) is almost here, and to help you get the most from the annual ship show, we've answered some common questions surrounding the event.  Read on for everything you need to know about the show, including where to go and how to participate in the upcoming Free Fly event. What is the IAE? The Intergalactic Aerospace Exposition (IAE) is the universe's premier spaceship convention. It provides everyone with the opportunity to see some of Star Citizen's most legendary ships and ground vehicles up close as different manufacturers showcase their finest in the expo center halls. And the best part? Nearly 200 ships and ground vehicles are yours to test-fly for free! Whether you're a seasoned pilot or just starting your journey, this is your chance to take the helm of the universe's most iconic rides.    When is the IAE taking place? The IAE takes place from November 20 through December 3.     What time does the event start? The IAE opens its gates on November 20 at 16:00 UTC.    When does the Free Fly start? The Free Fly will start on November 20, simultaneously with the launch of IAE, and will end on December 3. I don't have a Star Citizen game package or in-game spacecraft. How do I travel to Orison for the event? For the duration of the IAE, every account has access to a Crusader Intrepid ship. After getting started, head to the nearest ASOP ship retrieval terminal to access it.    Where does the IAE take place? Where do I have to go? For the first time ever, the IAE is being held at the Vision Center in Orison, on the planet Crusader, bringing the universe's premier aerospace expo to one of the most breathtaking cities in the Stanton system.    How do I get to the Vision Center? First, head to the planet Crusader. If this is your first visit to the Stanton system, you can choose to spawn at the Green Circle hab by selecting it as your primary residence.   If you're already a citizen, quantum travel to Crusader, spline jump to Orison, and then land at the August Dunlow Spaceport. From there, leave your hangar, and look out for signs for IAE. Follow the signs to the Vision Center and head into the expo. What ships are available to fly for free? Each day of the IAE, there will be different ships available for you to test-fly. Check out the full Manufacturer Schedule for details.      How do I rent a ship? In the expo center halls, you'll find ships on display from a variety of manufacturers throughout the event. If something catches your eye, head over to the Traveler Rentals terminals in the main IAE hall during that vehicle’s Manufacturer Day and follow the on-screen prompts to take it for a spin.   In addition to the ships on the show floor, each Manufacturer Day also unlocks a wider selection of flyable ships, some of which aren't on display but are still available to rent through the terminals. Manufacturers cycle almost every day, so be sure to check back often! You can visit the full schedule to play your test flights.  You can then head to the space port or any other ASOP terminal throughout the 'verse.   How long can ships be rented? Once you have rented a ship or vehicle, it will be available for 48 hours.    How many vehicles can be rented? You can rent every flyable or drivable vehicle exhibited at the IAE. Each ship or vehicle can be rented once.    Which ships get the Best in Show paints? All four ships that made it into the semi-finals of the recent Ship Showdown 2955 event (RSI Polaris, Anvil Asgard, RSI Zeus Mk II ES, Anvil Gladiator) will receive the limited-edition Best in Show livery as well as their in-game manufacturer poster. These are available to all players with these ships in their hangars. Additionally, the Polaris will receive a collectible in-game championship pennant to commemorate the glory of being this year's Ship Showdown champion.   If you already have one of these ships, you'll receive the IAE-exclusive paint (and extra items) following the last day of the event at no cost. To be eligible to receive the paints, the specific Best in Show ships, and not variants, need to be in your web-hangar at the end of IAE (having them in your Buyback List won't grant you the Best in Show paints). If you melt any of the ships before receiving the associated paints, then you will no longer be eligible.   Everyone pledging for a Best in Show (BIS) ship during the IAE will receive the paint and items, too. If you don't already have the ship, the vehicles will be bundled with the prizes during the Best in Show days following the 29th of November. Please note that these Best in Show Edition bundles already contain the BIS paints and posters within them and will not grant the standalone versions of those items.   The Best in Show ships will also be available to fly for free between November 29 and December 3.    I missed previous opportunities—how can I pledge for the Anvil F8C Lightning? Previously, pledging for an Anvil F8C Lightning required players to locate a CDF F8C Certification Pass (commonly referred to as a Gold License) and redeem it at an in-game rental kiosk. These licenses were only obtainable during select in-game events.   Starting with IAE 2955, the Gold Licenses will no longer be required. The F8C Lightning will be available to all players for pledge. Please note that the F8C Lightning is still limited to ONE per account, so if you have previously pledged for one, you will not be able to pledge for a second.   That said, we want to celebrate two groups of players: those who've redeemed a Gold License and previously unlocked pledge access, and those who've reached the qualifying Concierge level ahead of Anvil Day during IAE. If you are in either group, you will receive a special commemorative "Nightweaver" livery, which will be distributed during Anvil Day. This paint is not giftable, and only 1 paint will be awarded to each eligible player.   Please note: This reward will not be retroactively applied in the future, i.e., players who reach the qualifying Concierge level (Wing Commander) after IAE will not receive the commemorative paint. What's new this IAE? For the first time in Star Citizen history, Twitch Drops are landing, and we've chosen IAE as the stage for their grand debut! Watch any Star Citizen stream for a total of four hours during IAE to unlock an exclusive full armor set. As long as the streamer has opted in to participate in the Twitch Drops campaign, you can just enjoy the show and claim your reward. For full details on how it works and how to link your accounts, check out this comm-link.   Is there anything else that's new this IAE? Yes. IAE 2955 is your final opportunity to pledge for certain ships at their current pricing. Sometime after the event, these ships will receive a price adjustment to reflect recent and upcoming development updates: MISC Hull A MISC Hull B Argo RAFT Gatac Railen If you've been considering adding one of these to your fleet, now is the perfect time to secure them before the adjustment takes effect.   Will there be Warbond Daily Deals available? Yes! Check back each day throughout the event to see what's available. Each Warbond Daily Deal will run for 24 hours only. This year's Finale (Nov 30, 16:00 UTC - Dec 3, 20:00 UTC) will include a refresh with new Warbond Deals that will feature only at this time for select manufacturers and a few select offers from prior days may return.    Will there be quantity stock-limited ships? Yes! Each stock-limited ship is limited to one per account and will be available in six waves to cover as many global time zones as possible. Please note that depending on your time zone, some waves may occur the next calendar day.   ▲ Wave 1 - 16:00 UTC ▲ Wave 2 - 20:00 UTC ▲ Wave 3 - 00:00 UTC  ▲ Wave 4 - 04:00 UTC (the following day) ▲ Wave 5 - 08:00 UTC (the following day) ▲ Wave 6 - 12:00 UTC (the following day)   ► Starting on Nov 20 (IAE Day 1): RSI Constellation Phoenix ► Starting on Nov 21 (IAE Day 2): Origin 890 Jump ► Starting on Nov 22 (IAE Day 3): Drake Kraken, Drake Kraken Privateer ► Starting on Nov 24 (IAE Day 5): MISC Hull E ► Starting on Nov 26 (IAE Day 7): Consolidated Outland Pioneer ► Starting on Nov 28 (IAE Day 9): Aegis Idris-P, Aegis Javelin     Do I need a copy of Star Citizen to enjoy the Intergalactic Aerospace Expo? No. For the duration of the event, anyone can play Star Citizen for free. All you need to do is visit the Play Now page and follow the instructions.    Can I invite a friend? Of course! All they need to do is visit the Play Now page, create an account, and jump into the game. Don't forget, using your referral code during account creation grants them an additional 50,000 UEC. And if they decide to stay after the Free Fly, you'll earn a referral point. Plus, this IAE, you and the friends you refer will receive extra referral bonuses - more details here!       I am a new player. Where do I get more info? The New Player Guide is a fantastic first stop with a plethora of tips on how to get started, and the Welcome Hub presents various tutorials to help you get off on the right foot navigating the 'verse. Star Citizen veterans act as informal guides for an ever-growing number of new players in the Guide System. The Knowledge Base answers the most frequent questions in articles that cover everything from how to create an account to character equipment.

All four ships that made it into the semi-finals of the recent Ship Showdown 2955 event (RSI Polaris, Anvil Asgard, RSI Zeus Mk II ES, Anvil Gladiator) will receive the limited-edition Best in Show livery as well as their in-game manufacturer poster. These are available to all players with these ships in their hangars. Additionally, the Polaris will receive a collectible in-game championship pennant to commemorate the glory of being this year's Ship Showdown champion. If you already have one of these ships, you'll receive the IAE-exclusive paint (and extra items) following the last day of the event at no cost. To be eligible to receive the paints, the specific Best in Show ships, and not variants, need to be in your web-hangar at the end of IAE (having them in your Buyback List won't grant you the Best in Show paints). If you melt any of the ships before receiving the associated paints, then you will no longer be eligible. Everyone pledging for a Best in Show (BIS) ship during the IAE will receive the paint and items, too. If you don't already have the ship, the vehicles will be bundled with the prizes during the Best in Show days following the 29th of November. Please note that these Best in Show Edition bundles already contain the BIS paints and posters within them and will not grant the standalone versions of those items. The Best in Show ships will also be available to fly for free between November 29 and December 3. I missed previous opportunities—how can I pledge for the Anvil F8C Lightning? Previously, pledging for an Anvil F8C Lightning required players to locate a CDF F8C Certification Pass (commonly referred to as a Gold License) and redeem it at an in-game rental kiosk. These licenses were only obtainable during select in-game events. Starting with IAE 2955, the Gold Licenses will no longer be required. The F8C Lightning will be available to all players for pledge. Please note that the F8C Lightning is still limited to ONE per account, so if you have previously pledged for one, you will not be able to pledge for a second. That said, we want to celebrate two groups of players: those who've redeemed a Gold License and previously unlocked pledge access, and those who've reached the qualifying Concierge level ahead of Anvil Day during IAE. If you are in either group, you will receive a special commemorative "Nightweaver" livery, which will be distributed during Anvil Day. This paint is not giftable, and only 1 paint will be awarded to each eligible player. Please note: This reward will not be retroactively applied in the future, i.e., players who reach the qualifying Concierge level (Wing Commander) after IAE will not receive the commemorative paint. What's new this IAE? For the first time in Star Citizen history, Twitch Drops are landing, and we've chosen IAE as the stage for their grand debut! Watch any Star Citizen stream for a total of four hours during IAE to unlock an exclusive full armor set. As long as the streamer has opted in to participate in the Twitch Drops campaign, you can just enjoy the show and claim your reward. For full details on how it works and how to link your accounts, check out this comm-link. Is there anything else that's new this IAE? Yes. IAE 2955 is your final opportunity to pledge for certain ships at their current pricing. Sometime after the event, these ships will receive a price adjustment to reflect recent and upcoming development updates: MISC Hull A MISC Hull B Argo RAFT Gatac Railen If you've been considering adding one of these to your fleet, now is the perfect time to secure them before the adjustment takes effect. Will there be Warbond Daily Deals available? Yes! Check back each day throughout the event to see what's available. Each Warbond Daily Deal will run for 24 hours only. This year's Finale (Nov 30, 16:00 UTC - Dec 3, 20:00 UTC) will include a refresh with new Warbond Deals that will feature only at this time for select manufacturers and a few select offers from prior days may return. Will there be quantity stock-limited ships? Yes! Each stock-limited ship is limited to one per account and will be available in six waves to cover as many global time zones as possible. Please note that depending on your time zone, some waves may occur the next calendar day. ▲ Wave 1 - 16:00 UTC ▲ Wave 2 - 20:00 UTC ▲ Wave 3 - 00:00 UTC ▲ Wave 4 - 04:00 UTC (the following day) ▲ Wave 5 - 08:00 UTC (the following day) ▲ Wave 6 - 12:00 UTC (the following day) ► Starting on Nov 20 (IAE Day 1): RSI Constellation Phoenix ► Starting on Nov 21 (IAE Day 2): Origin 890 Jump ► Starting on Nov 22 (IAE Day 3): Drake Kraken, Drake Kraken Privateer ► Starting on Nov 24 (IAE Day 5): MISC Hull E ► Starting on Nov 26 (IAE Day 7): Consolidated Outland Pioneer ► Starting on Nov 28 (IAE Day 9): Aegis Idris-P, Aegis Javelin Do I need a copy of Star Citizen to enjoy the Intergalactic Aerospace Expo? No. For the duration of the event, anyone can play Star Citizen for free. All you need to do is visit the Play Now page and follow the instructions. Can I invite a friend? Of course! All they need to do is visit the Play Now page, create an account, and jump into the game. Don't forget, using your referral code during account creation grants them an additional 50,000 UEC. And if they decide to stay after the Free Fly, you'll earn a referral point. Plus, this IAE, you and the friends you refer will receive extra referral bonuses - more details here! I am a new player. Where do I get more info? The New Player Guide is a fantastic first stop with a plethora of tips on how to get started, and the Welcome Hub presents various tutorials to help you get off on the right foot navigating the 'verse. Star Citizen veterans act as informal guides for an ever-growing number of new players in the Guide System. The Knowledge Base answers the most frequent questions in articles that cover everything from how to create an account to character equipment.

title: Re: Does Star Citizen have occlusion culling?
summary: GPU-side culling can be nicer (you get to use fresher data) but means you can't cut work on CPU based on the result. For instance, with the CPU system we can avoid submitting shadow calculations for lights that aren't visible. Modern APIs like Vulkan add some flexible features that help with GPU-driven command-generation, but fully switching to GPU culling would mean moving a lot of stuff we currently do on CPU to the GPU just so that we'd be able to skip the culled ones. I probably shouldn't try to give any more detail than that because it's not my special area. Worth mentioning though that we also do frustum and portal culling on the CPU, so it's not like we'd be cull-less if we had GPU-only occlusion culling. In the end it all comes down to trade-offs.

title: Re: A petition for pistols
summary: Just want to stress I'm looking at this from a content POV, not a feature POV currently of saying 'add this thing', it's more looking at what can be done within the existing params.  Medgun is currently too good but the alternative to healing is medpens which we've seen swapping to can lead to weapon drops and such I don't want to nerf the medgun until some of those bugs are fixed (biggest offender is being looked at currently). Once that is done I can look into toning it down  I think it competing with pistols is fine as once things like armour come online, you wanting to always take heavy and always having access to two primary slots becomes less of a crutch.   It's another reason why injuries were made to be more 'long term look after yourself' so it's less always getting them in short combat bursts so you feel you have to suppress them   But overall the ease of access with the medgun being tied to a pistol slot is preferable just from a single input press which was not an attempt to 'nerf it' but make it a meaningful choice and actually compete against something but the key reason was the consistent keybind (I know about the knife slot, that was not something that was intended)   Adding another hotkey in a game with so many already is just extra complications I want to avoid as keeping it intuitive is really important    But to summaries, aware of how strong the medgun is  want to ensure using med pens isn't frustrating / causes issues before looking at tuning it down (BDL increase, slower healing, not a crazy ammo capacity, etc) currently you do a lot of 'small skirmish in a fight, heal' rinse repeat which I don't think is great   There's a lot of things we can do from a feature POV but from a content POV those changes need some bug fixes

title: Re: MFDs tank performances and make the game unplayable
summary: Hi!  Thanks @nurseman for the tag.   So I’ve not looked at MFDs in the live release recently, nor am I on the UI team, however I can probably help fill in a few blanks.    The live release still uses Scaleform as the actual UI rendering system, and this is almost exclusively driven by our own UI authoring tool (Building Blocks) rather than Flash.   The reason Scaleform is still in use is because the new engine tech hasn’t been integrated into the live release for quite some time, as the focus has been on stability, content, and improving the quality of the of life for players, and large tech changes can risk that (you can find some of my older posts for details rather than us rehashing that here).   However our new UI rendering system called Paint is in now the default in our main branch and will be coming to the live release soon (I can’t answer when, it’s tied to many other decisions). This is already proving to be faster, less intensive on CPU, and easier to optimise. However UI remains a cost in SC due to the many in-world UI screens, holograms, and effects. As such its the focus of further major optimisations by the UI Tech team at the moment.   If there are follow up questions please bear in mind I’m not deeply involved with the UI side of things.   Cheers  Ali Brown

title: Re: Engineering Questions
summary: Hi  Before I answer your question want to use the opportunity and thank all for all the videos, feedback and discussions around the gameplay. It already helps us tremendously to improve the feature.  Not as fast as I and probably you like, but it is important for us that we set a good base to build on.  To your questions:  I cannot promise anything here sadly. We are currently focusing on getting the "flow" right. Means damage, fire and repair is our main focus to get a nice mix of good gameplay and fullfilling the Star Citizen Fantasy. So until we are "happy enough" we wont add anything new to the mix. Reason is we really need to focus on as few things as possible to not "water down" the feedback. Thank you for asking that since I saw already some posts and IC reports around it. So let me clarify. (Trying to do a TLDR version here) Also what you see here is what we want to go forward with. Relay rework clarification Relays are still the connectors of all ship components, but if you lose all the fuses inside items will not lose the connection anymore. The reason here is that some ships are just build in a way that the relay that connects all items or is critical are just too easy of a target. Hence we did decide to rework the system. What happens now is that each relay has still fuses inside. Once all fuses are destroyed or depleted, the relay will go into a "red" state. The "red" state of the relay means that it will block some power.  This means: If you have lost a relay (by it not having any fuses anymore) the available power in the ship will drop.  Depending on the ship size and the amount of relays present that can have a significant impact on your ship. So they are still an important factor to be taken care of.  3. Yes, patch by patch.  Cheers,

title: Re: Don't nerf high risk, high reward gameplay, please.
summary: Howdy,    I can speak some to the logic and plans behind the changes to commodity prices, size availability and ROI/Profit Lines. Most of those numbers are what I focus on in the Econ team. I'm also going to speak on these points to a level that a lot of people's eyes will glaze over and need to watch someone else to summarize it. Sorry. As always, a lot of upcoming content that are in the works for SC will have a big scale affect on the overall goals of trading, sandbox resource gathering, and the economy as a whole. So any specifics I might go into here is only about the current state of balance for trade, not what they will be once other majer features change that landscape, which they absolutely will.  Why does Partillium get another nerf in PTU?  Well, you might not have noticed yet, (that's not a slight on you, I'm well aware of the current state on communicating information about trade goods and more.) We actually clamped down all commodities in terms of the availability sizes this patch, not specifically partillium. What you will find is that aside from a few special exceptions(Osoian hides, atlassium, etc), most commodities will fall into the following "brackets" in terms of availability.  32/24SCU (some outposts can't support 32 SCU crates),  16SCU, 8SCU, and 2SCU.     The value per SCU goes up the lower the bracket.  It's actually intended to be a pain point for ships with excessively large grids to try and fill up with crates that are below their bracket range. We don't outright block them of course. this is a sandbox and going outside the limits is allowed, but a good sandbox does have friction and makes the world respond that way when you try to push the boundaries of the normal flow.    CIG should be boosting ROI across the board on all commodities.  We actually did this in 4.4 too! Although since it's only the first part of a larger increase to sandbox values it won't feel quite as strong in just 4.4. as it will with the rest of the changes coming out. Most tradable resources in 4.4 now have at least some pair of locations that can get you to about a 20% Discount on purchase and a 35% premium on sale in the perfect conditions. (The lower along the value by bracket you go, the more locations there are to give you those good prices and vice versa.) Depending on how you calculate it, that's... "Slightly above a 68%" return on investments. (Take any values with a grain of salt, there's a LOT of layers of dynamic calculation that modulate the end point prices you will actually see in-game, and literally every location has another set of values in place that can either add or subtract to those bands.)   The ROI is 7-16% after the nerf last patch... (best case scenario)  It's actually not, Partillium's locations do have some of those aforementioned modifiers that change the possible best end ROI to a 10% Discount and a 25% Premium. instead of 20/35. But the reason you still aren't seeing that benefit is that it's oversaturated at the locations. The more players focus on a single commodity the worse those places prices get for all players, that's part of the current working effects of the dynamic price changes based on demand. If everyone focuses Partillium for instance, even that reduced potential 33% ROI can drop all the way to 7-8% ROI. This leads us into the reason that Partillium got hit in the prior patch.  So the goal for the way the balance between the "chase" commodities in their bracket is intended to work, is that even if one resource is at first the most profitable: If too many people focus on that resource, it's profit lines drop below the 2nd, then 3rd, then 4th best options. This creates a rolling meta where there should never really just be one single commodity that is inherently the "best choice".  That's healthy for the game, and makes the balance between other traders, and pirates a lot more of a mind game as opposed to just camping the specifically best commodity.   For example, In the 2 SCU bracket, the 2nd best option behind partillium is diamond laminate(~84k).  Before the nerf of partillium from ~190k to ~90k, at 190k, no matter how many players focused on partillium, diamond laminate would never overtake it as the best option, this isn't healthy for the sandbox as a whole, it becomes the only thing worth trading and all the locations you can get partillium become death traps, (which they absolutely were, and still honestly are a bit more than I'd like.) That's the motivation behind why we dropped partillium to a closer value for its bracket.    Just as a little bonus:  Here are some other currently intended "chase" commodities at the top of their brackets: fresh food, tritium and dymantium at 8SCU, Bioplastic, Widow, Diamond and Gold at 16 SCU, and lastly pressurized ice, steel, tungsten and dynaflex at the 24/32SCU bracket. One of the benefits we want to make of having bigger ships, is that you will have enough space to trade these chase goods of higher brackets for a better profit line, which smaller ships don't see similar profit lines for.   Making these brackets a bit easier to quickly identify is one of the reasons we chose to shift many commodities like partillium to 2scu as well.    Ok, so that's the points I want to clarify for why we decided to bring Partillium in line with the rest of the goods. Now lets talk about the parts where you guys are right:     As another commenter said:  Sandbox gameplay even low risk sandbox gameplay should have better payout.  Yep, you are right. Stay tuned for more on this in the next couple patches.  Honestly, I wouldn't have been able to justify any kind of universal buff to sandbox commodities while Partillium was still that much of an outlier. Now that it's closer in line to the other 2scu chase commodities... whatever buffs and changes will happen on a per-bracket basis and include partillium, instead of treating it as an outlier of that bracket.  If you want to nerf something, nerf these zero risk high reward contracted cargo missions.   I would just very much like to clarify, I don't like... wake up in the morning and say "Y'know what? I'm in a Nerfing mood today, what can I hit?".  I'm really trying not to crack a joke here, but genuinely, it's a pretty elaborate discussion for the team when we bring up a need to nerf something, even when it seems like the data shows it's a good call.   All of this lead's to very boring game play that encourages murder hobos Yeah. There's some contributing factors from other in progress systems here, but we know that this is an especially harsh factor for people mining, salvaging and trading, since those are currently the most piratable goods, and even those are well below piracy values. (not including player trading market values) to make it feel actually worth it.

summary: Were supposed to be PUNISHED into LOWER TIER COMMODITIES  Shouldn't really reply to this kind of comment. But I'll give you some clarification, because I wasn't clear enough.   No. You aren't punished for having a bigger ship.  The goal of each bracket of commodity is this:   A ship that can carry 20 32SCU crates, will make like 20% more than: A ship that can carry 20 16 SCU crates, Which makes 20% more than a ship that carries 20 8 SCU crates, which makes 20% more than a ship that carries 20 2 SCU crates. Which still makes good UEC, since, as you pointed out, they have invested value into a risk for their profits.    The goal here is that the Ship that carries 320 2scu crates, isn't making 16x what the smallest ship is making.  but they ARE making more, each time you buy a bigger ship and move to a new bracket, you should be able to pick if moving up and making a better TOTAL volume/uec haul is better for your ships size, or if you should continue to compete at the lower bracket to make the best money.   but the lower cargo grid ships, will NOT be able to access the same total volume per haul that makes the larger brackets worthwhile.  Even if there's enough supply and demand that moving 4000 SCU of Steel at a time is valuable, the requirements of a grid to really hit that price point is too high for ships of only 100SCU.    I didn't mean to imply that larger ships wouldn't be getting access to better trade routes and significantly better total profit lines. But those are going to be different resources than the guy flying from outpost to outpost moving their rarest goods.

summary: Yeah, you've got it basically right. This was one of the reasons we wanted to clamp the availability of scu which you can buy commodoties at into these brackets. To make it a bit clearer to see where the breakpoints at.   For instance, Tritium near the top of the 8SCU bracket, which is on average around 13k/SCU, vs Combboard, the bottom of the 2 SCU bracket at 15K/SCU.  when you are looking at these prices and the Supply/Demand calculation is running, it's really hard to track that these are different brackets. title: Re: CIG changed Reclaimer description on sale page, no more on board processing
summary: Hey folks, Disco Here. :wave:  So, we've begun a slow audit process of the entire store to identify key elements that haven't been highlighted that should be, better define some terms that have been nebulous for awhile, and correct outright errors when needed.  As part of this process, we added a new formalized definition of what the term "Heavy Salvage" means for a ship into a box that is built to only display three elements. These three elements are NEVER reflective of the entire story for any given ship, but in this instance, there was a better choice to be made on which one of the three couldn't be displayed.  So we've removed the more fluffy line above and restored the refinery mention with unchanged, salient details, still reflective of the ship.  That said, I want to remind everyone that this bullet point box has never, nor will ever, reflect every aspect of the ship or vehicle. It's simply a place for some highlights, and we've now restored the better highlight listing. :+1:

title: Re: Don't nerf high risk, high reward gameplay, please.
summary: This leaves a specific place for multicrew actually. Because of the existence of "Downtrading."  Remember how I said we don't hardlimit the brackets? We just make it a bit harder to safely and efficiently load up ships with those goods in a timely manner?   Well... If you have some extra people along, then you can overcome that barrier pretty easily.  So sure, it might be a pain for ONE person to load a Cat with 40 8SCU crates, even if you have to grab 2-3 different commodities in that bracket.   It might even be dangerous for a solo player in a cat to do that, it could take them like 20 Minutes!   But, if you have a crew... then you can start venturing into more risky and lower brackets of cargo than you should be safe trading on your own.   And if you have a crew or have hired a guard for instance. You also have a protection against the "Treasure Ship" scenario, which would be if you have loaded up so much high value goods on your ship, that you become the golden lootbox for all pirates in the system. You are much more free to do that if you have guards, and can pay them part of the excess value you are getting from downtrading.   Just also expect that you will be making enemies of all the small ships trying to trade there, because you are a big fish, invading their small pond.  A 1 Crew Cateripillar trying to compete and load up at a small outpost moving a few different 2 SCU bracket goods is going to get obliterated. partially because of how long it takes you to solo load it. But a Full Crew Cat, with maybe 1 or two guards?  Well.... You might be able to do some of that dangerous downtrading, and sure you might need to stop at a few locations to fully load up. But suddenly, a ship of 4-6 crew. Running Low Bracket goods? It's incredibly high risk, but if you are willing to go against the grain for it, it might be worth it.   I honestly, think that these brackets actually make it MORE rewarding, not less for multicrew ships, because the MAIN factor that's making it hard to downtrade is offset by having more people on the ship.

title: Alpha 4.4.0 - Welcome to Nyx
summary: Hi everyone,  Following the release of Pyro last year, new Jump Points have been found, leading to our third system: Nyx!  For some, this is a homecoming. For others, it is a new frontier built on stubborn pride and hard-won independence. Levski has always stood apart, and its people have every intention of keeping it that way.  Explore the Grand Barter and meet the locals. Visit the new hospital, either out of curiosity or by misfortune. Check out the Teach's Ship Shop and see what the old-timers have to offer. Miners and freight crews will find plenty of work in Nyx, as new exterior freight elevators are coming to the major stations in our systems and new interstellar hauling missions are pushing the limits of long-range supply routes.  But don't get too comfortable. Activity along the fringes of Nyx has stirred something in the dark. Early reports suggest Vanduul scouts are testing the edges of the system. Nothing has been confirmed yet, but everyone knows how these stories typically begin and end. Star Citizen Alpha 4.4.0: Welcome to Nyx is now available. Time to touch down, settle in, and write the next chapter together! title: [4.4.0 LIVE] Nyx System
summary: Greetings!  The Nyx System has been introduced in 4.4.0, which includes the returning Levski settlement, Delamar, Glaciem ring asteroid belt, QV Service stations, Jump Points and more! title: [4.4.0 LIVE] Interstellar Hauling Missions
summary: Greetings!  Alpha 4.4.0 has implemented interstellar hauling missions that start in one system and finish in another, offering longer-distance cargo hauling for you to take on. These missions are procedurally generated across the Stanton, Pyro, and Nyx systems that route goods from one system to another. They come in a variety of shapes and sizes, for players with various ships, law alignments, and session expectations.  We look forward to hearing your thoughts, and thanks for taking the time!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: [4.4.0 LIVE] Ballistic Missile Launcher "Boomtube"
summary: Greetings!  A new Ballistic Missile Launcher has been added in 4.4.0, the "Boomtube". This launcher consists of three rockets tapped together in a tube releasing this single deadly payload. The Design intent with this weapon is a high power explosive with a singular magazine, finding the sweet spot between being close enough to deal with the weapons inaccuracies but not close enough to trigger a dud (arming distance).  We look forward to hearing your thoughts, and thanks for taking the time!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: [4.4.0 LIVE] Sworn Enemies Operation
summary: Greetings!  InterSec is looking for contractors willing to investigate abandoned QV Logistics stations to follow the trail of Vanduul tech that was sold to ASD. Only those with multiple ranks of reputation with InterSec will be  trusted with this information. We look forward to hearing your thoughts, and thanks for taking the time!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: Roadmap Roundup - November 19, 2025
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.  With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!  -CIG Community Team Release View 4.4.0 All 4.4.0 cards have been set to Released.  MaxOx Neutron Cannon Art Refactors Updating several MaxOx Neutron Cannons' art style and geometry: Size 1 and 2. :scroll: Size 3 has been postponed and will be introduced in a future update.   4.5.0 Engineering Introducing dedicated engineering roles aboard ships, allowing players to actively manage power distribution, repairs, and system efficiency in real time. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Fire Hazards Bringing fire hazards to ships and environments, along with Fire Extinguisher mechanics, requiring players to manage and extinguish blazes before they spread. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Physical Helmets Implementing physical helmets in the persistent universe. Pick one up, rotate it, inspect every detail, carry it around, attach it to your hip, or toss it across a room if you want. When you equip a helmet, you put on or remove the same one you held in your hands, complete with a fully realized interior. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  New Barrel Attachments Implementing a host of new barrel attachments with scorched/tweaker power levels, as well as a new tactical VOLT flashlight. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Vulkan Renderer Improvements Increasing both the stability and speed of the Vulkan renderer, with many crash fixes, diagnostic improvements, and multi-threaded render-submission, while adding support for HDR and NVidia's DLSS Transformer model. Also included is an overhaul to the Graphics Options, with many new settings, and a VRAM bar to help players configure the graphics for their GPU. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  FPS AI Improvements Implementing improvements to FPS combat AI for smarter decision making, refined perception, and more reliable reactions in combat. This includes better cover use, grenade targeting, friend or foe checks, group awareness, and animation sync support to make encounters feel more tactical and responsive. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  New Hairstyles (4.5.0) Adding three additional hairstyles, and one new facial hair customization for your character. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.

title: IAE 2955 - Showtime! Contest
summary: The Intergalactic Aerospace Expo 2955 has landed, and this year, we’re challenging you to capture your favorite ships and vehicles in action. It’s Showtime!  Show us how you’re mastering your ship, how you’re fighting enemies, loading cargo, salvaging, mining or any gameplay that you have in mind while enjoying the vehicles presented during the IAE 2955. How To Participate We’re calling on the community to celebrate the IAE 2955 by showcasing their eye for detail and cinematic flair.  Please read the ⁠⁠contest rules carefully to avoid disqualification. :brain: Prepare: Choose your favorite ship or vehicle and plan an exciting hero shot, solo or with others. :camera_with_flash: Capture: Take the screenshot in-game. Feel free to take the vehicle for a spin, as you can rent them for free during IAE 2955! :outbox_tray: Submit: Send your entry to the ⁠⁠Community Hub by submitting your entry to the dedicated Showtime! category. You can submit multiple entries, so enjoy the many manufacturers present during the event from November 20 to December 3rd!   Keep In Mind! Read the contest rules. Posts must be submitted to the Community Hub, entitled “Showtime! IAE 2955”, and select the Image category. You can do so by clicking on "Create an Event Post". Each submission must feature a “hero shot” of your ship or vehicle in action. Post-processing effects are not allowed. AI-generated or AI-edited content is not allowed. Replies to this thread will NOT count as a submission. Group submissions are not allowed, but feel free to feature multiple players in action in your image. Only the person posting the image can win a prize. Multiple  submissions are allowed, but please limit them to a maximum of five of your highest-quality shots (this is not a hard-and-fast rule).   Winning Conditions The CIG jury will judge your submissions on the following: Quality Creativity and composition Hero shot, create an iconic or memorable moment   Dates The submission period ends on Wednesday, December 3, 2025, 20:00 UTC.   Rewards :first_place_medal: 1st Place: Anvil Paladin in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Carmine" Livery :second_place_medal: 2nd Place: Esperia Stinger in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Black Widow" Livery :third_place_medal: 3rd Place: RSI Apollo Triage in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Delphi" Livery :sports_medal: 4th Place: Grey’s Shiv in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Blue Blossom" Livery :sports_medal: 5th Place: RSI Salvation in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Vespid" Livery Winners :first_place_medal: 1st Place: @ln_nova, we love the composition! So simple, yet so complex, your exploration theme backed with the star and just two elements, a citizen and their Clipper, has won our hearts! Can you do the same with your newly earned Paladin? :second_place_medal: 2nd Place: @DriftwoodBadger, your challenge was too easy, so we're sending you a Stinger to up your combat adventures! :third_place_medal: 3rd Place: @IAmSpekter, what a shot! Just the right amount of blurriness to capture the new Perseus along with the Epoque Aves armor and the Epoque Geist helmet, in the harsh and cold environment. You've earned yourself an Apollo Triage to heal your wounds. :sports_medal: 4th Place: @Irmdall, You perfectly captured the Gunner role, and directly targeted our hearts! Please, leave the Clipper alone. We'll send you a Shiv to make it up to you! :sports_medal: 5th Place: @ElIndio, IT IS FORBIDDEN TO MOCK ARCHIBALD HURSTON! But it was actually quite funny, to be honest. For this... you're sent on new missions with your brand-new Salvation!

title: Star Citizen Alpha 4.4.0 LIVE - Hotfix Central (Updated 11.26.2025)
summary: Hi Everyone!  Time again for another Hotfix Central thread to keep you all up to date on things going on outside of the normal patch cycle in SC Alpha 4.4.0 LIVE! This will be a living document of all the hotfixes applied to the current LIVE environment, along with dates as a timeline and when the HOTFIX channel is open and closed.  These posts will be locked down to comments as the updates will span the entire 4.4.x cycle so please check out the issue council and testing chats for any information you would like to let us know about!  Current 4.4.0 LIVE Status | 11.26.2025     Status: Hotfix Channel Currently Closed     Latest LIVE Client CL: 10766222      Latest LIVE DGS CL: 10733565 (10766222 Canaried onto some LIVE shards for testing) ► 11.26.2025: Hotfix 10766222 DGS/Client is now on the LIVE channel with further QT related client crash fixes (client) and fixes for Hull-C automated cargo loading freezing (DGS)  ► 11.24.2025: 10762541 Small client hotfix on the HOTFIX channel for mission caching optimizations ► 11.24.2025: 10753606 currently on LIVE - Client Side: Audio performance fixes (won't fully fix stuttering) and further performance optimizations for Levski. - DGS Side: Multiple DGS crash fixes, "Vanduul-Tech Smugglers" auxiliary station laptop with the code is missing. ► 11.20.2025: 10744215 Client Hotfix is currently out on LIVE with fixes for free fly accounts getting locked when setting spawn to Nyx stations   Using the HOTFIX channel The HOTFIX channel will become available for periods of time when the client-side of the game needs the hotfix. This channel will point to the LIVE environment and using this will retain and add progress to your LIVE account as if you were playing normally. The best way to play on HOTFIX is to rename your LIVE folder to HOTFIX and verify using the HOTFIX channel on the launcher. Reverse this process to go back to LIVE once it is released or you would like to stop using this channel.

title: Re: Player stuck in shard after repair
summary: We have that on our radar as well. They may or may no be related. Currently the 41013 is happening way more, and sometimes multiple bugs will report to the same error. Usually what ends up happening with cases like this where there are multiple disconnection errors stacking on top of each other is that we will fix the worst one, and see if it takes down any of the others with it. Then we focus on the worst of whatever is left after that.

title: Re: AMD GI-1.2
summary: While it can sound appealing to just use the sample version unmodified, there are definitely trade-offs that they've made that affect things like responsiveness and stability that we wouldn't have been able to change easily, as well as errors in their code that we've fixed.  On top of that, there's quite a lot of stuff that's game dependent, for instance we want the surface lighting calculation to work similarly to the main lighting pass, so we have to have our own shader there so it can read shadows, mask out lights by area, etc. Finally there's the performance aspect. We're in the optimization phase now and I'm chopping and rewriting all sorts of things to try to get the frame time down. That's a lot easier when it's all CIG code and we can move passes around, merge or split shaders, change internal formats and so on.

Mission Content / UI - Patrol Mission progress halts after reaching location markers PU - Pyro - Storm Breaker - Locations / Missions - Opened safes remain open after 2 hour cooldown   Features & Gameplay Gameplay Updates Engineering Gameplay Introducing dedicated engineering roles aboard ships, allowing players to actively manage power distribution, repairs, and system efficiency in real time. The overall goal and experience with this Engineering update should see ships behaving approximately as well as 4.4.0 in combat and surviveability with the added bonus of engineering and multi-crew to extend this beyond the capabilities of 4.4. Beyond this, players may need to check on their ship between battles to make necessary repairs so that they are fully prepared for their next encounter.  This introduces numerous updates to all ships and vehicles with the initial implementation of ship armor loads of updates to heat, power, and life support management, diagnostic and engineering screens, large sweeping changes to ship component health, damage resistances, and heat generation, hull health and weapon balancing, as well as updating the repair tools needed for the job.  Since the previous Tech-Preview, we have made dozens of fixes as well as updates for balance and UI and further updates for more vehicles. Deactivated fire for bullet hits as well as overheating of powerplants, increased coolant provided by the coolers, reduced critical powerplant failure point, updated armor to have health again, fixes to ballistic cooldowns, reducing radar heat, and ship health now tied to critical health. As this new update affects every ship and vehicle in the game, many further updates and balancing will be down during the coarse of the PTU phases for 4.5 and beyond.  Ship Fire Hazards Bringing fire hazards to ships and environments, along with Fire Extinguisher mechanics, requiring players to manage and extinguish blazes before they spread. This includes retrievable fire extinguishers aboard ships that have a limited use before needing to be recharged. Weapons and Items Physical Helmets Implementing physical helmets in the persistent universe. Pick one up, rotate it, inspect every detail, carry it around, attach it to your hip, or toss it across a room if you want. When you equip a helmet, you put on or remove the same one you held in your hands, complete with a fully realized interior.
