title: Re: [4.5.0 PTU] Updated Engineering Gameplay
summary: Hi all,  Thank you all for all the feedback that we have been recieving, especially in the last couple of days. Before I provide a summary of the recent updates, I want to mention few things first. We will soon publish a guide that will give in-depth information about Engineering Gameplay, including giving an insight on future changes.   Naturally, we're also still in active development for the Engineering Gameplay feature as stated in the ISC, and as frustrating it might sound for some, this requires a lot of iteration to get right (especially in our PTU testing environment).  For example, the armour system currently is one of the systems that we'll iterate on quite heavily moving forward, like implementing thresholds so that smaller caliber projectiles cannot damage or penetrate stronger armor.   Let's talk about TTD / TTK and a little bit about the shield topic since both topics caused some confusion.   You will have noticed we went through various changes throughout this PTU cycle, but fundamentally, we still want ships to be disabled more often than them exploding. We still want to allow players to have access to all the gameplay that comes with disabled ships. It also still stands true that experiencing a critical failure or your ship exploding will be mainly driven by the state of the power plant.  Currently implemented, there are four scenarios where a ship can explode, aka hard death: 1. If Power Plant goes critical after being destroyed and the player fails to repair or remove it in a given amount of time, which is Power Plant dependent. This shouldn't happen all the time.  2. If one critical part of the ship is destroyed aka is at 0 health, has a chance to cause the Power Plant to experience a critical failure, like in the first example. Players will still have the option to counter act this by repairing or removing the Power Plant within the given amount of time.  3. If one the ship is hit by a very powerful projectile that does do a lot of damage the ship will directly explode. An Idris Railgun hit should still take out an Arrow in a single hit.  4.If all critical parts are destroyed and the ship is still being shot at persistently, the ship will at some point will be fully destroyed and explode. Currently this is tuned to require 10x the hull damage before this occurs, but is subject to further balance.  As you can tell there is no guarantee for ships to always explode and we want players to have the opportunity to perform field repairs or board disabled ships. The chance of a ship exploding through critical power plant failure overall is lower than 30%, though, we have seen some bugs here that the explosions occur more often than they should, which we are working on to get them fixed. However, we still want to adhere to established design goals, such as extremely strong weapons having the ability to do serious damage to lighter and less armoured ships, or even take them out in single hits. And though the patch notes yesterday shared the changes we did around the Ship Overkill mechanic did not go into enough detail, we fundamentally want to prevent scenarios were disabled ships are quasi-invulnerable without negating existing gameplay loops like piracy or component salvage. The above is emulating some of the highly detailed physical damage simulation that Maelstrom will eventually bring to Star Citizen. Parts will have structural integrity, and will at some point no longer be able to withstand sustained damage and break apart.  To summarize: Ships should be disabled a lot more often than explode. Critical failures should still allow you to recover and escape Disabled ships can still explode if enough damage is applied   As for shields, we are still working on a fix that causes redundant shields not to auto activate for ships with more than two shield generators. Additionally, the patch notes from yesterday made it sound as if recently we made drastic changes to shield behavior, when in reality the update was meant to convey how it already functions in 4.4.0. Currently, all shield generators contribute to the overall health pool of the shield, but only the powered shield generators contribute to the shield recharge rate.    We really appreciate all of your feedback and I guarantee you that we hear you. We review and digest your feedback daily, have passionate discussions about how to best address your concers.  I hope you understand that we can't reply to all posts, but we do read them and our excellent Player Experience team is constantly in touch with you all to keep us in check. We knew that the release of Engineering would be a challenge and that due to the amount of the changes we've introduced it can be even trickier to get things right. Some of the balance changes we did early in this PTU cycle have been temporarily reverted to ensure we have a more stable base to balance and eliminate factors that could cause unforseen edge cases. As mentioned during the recent ISC, Engineering Gameplay is here to stay and we will do our best to work with you all and make it the best it can be.    Cheers,
body_html: Hi all, Thank you all for all the feedback that we have been recieving, especially in the last couple of days. Before I provide a summary of the recent updates, I want to mention few things first. We will soon publish a guide that will give in-depth information about Engineering Gameplay, including giving an insight on future changes. Naturally, we're also still in active development for the Engineering Gameplay feature as stated in the ISC, and as frustrating it might sound for some, this requires a lot of iteration to get right (especially in our PTU testing environment). For example, the armour system currently is one of the systems that we'll iterate on quite heavily moving forward, like implementing thresholds so that smaller caliber projectiles cannot damage or penetrate stronger armor. Let's talk about TTD / TTK and a little bit about the shield topic since both topics caused some confusion. You will have noticed we went through various changes throughout this PTU cycle, but fundamentally, we still want ships to be disabled more often than them exploding. We still want to allow players to have access to all the gameplay that comes with disabled ships. It also still stands true that experiencing a critical failure or your ship exploding will be mainly driven by the state of the power plant. Currently implemented, there are four scenarios where a ship can explode, aka hard death: 1. If Power Plant goes critical after being destroyed and the player fails to repair or remove it in a given amount of time, which is Power Plant dependent. This shouldn't happen all the time. 2. If one critical part of the ship is destroyed aka is at 0 health, has a chance to cause the Power Plant to experience a critical failure, like in the first example. Players will still have the option to counter act this by repairing or removing the Power Plant within the given amount of time. 3. If one the ship is hit by a very powerful projectile that does do a lot of damage the ship will directly explode. An Idris Railgun hit should still take out an Arrow in a single hit. 4.If all critical parts are destroyed and the ship is still being shot at persistently, the ship will at some point will be fully destroyed and explode. Currently this is tuned to require 10x the hull damage before this occurs, but is subject to further balance. As you can tell there is no guarantee for ships to always explode and we want players to have the opportunity to perform field repairs or board disabled ships. The chance of a ship exploding through critical power plant failure overall is lower than 30%, though, we have seen some bugs here that the explosions occur more often than they should, which we are working on to get them fixed. However, we still want to adhere to established design goals, such as extremely strong weapons having the ability to do serious damage to lighter and less armoured ships, or even take them out in single hits. And though the patch notes yesterday shared the changes we did around the Ship Overkill mechanic did not go into enough detail, we fundamentally want to prevent scenarios were disabled ships are quasi-invulnerable without negating existing gameplay loops like piracy or component salvage. The above is emulating some of the highly detailed physical damage simulation that Maelstrom will eventually bring to Star Citizen. Parts will have structural integrity, and will at some point no longer be able to withstand sustained damage and break apart. To summarize: Ships should be disabled a lot more often than explode. Critical failures should still allow you to recover and escape Disabled ships can still explode if enough damage is applied As for shields, we are still working on a fix that causes redundant shields not to auto activate for ships with more than two shield generators. Additionally, the patch notes from yesterday made it sound as if recently we made drastic changes to shield behavior, when in reality the update was meant to convey how it already functions in 4.4.0. Currently, all shield generators contribute to the overall health pool of the shield, but only the powered shield generators contribute to the shield recharge rate. We really appreciate all of your feedback and I guarantee you that we hear you. We review and digest your feedback daily, have passionate discussions about how to best address your concers. I hope you understand that we can't reply to all posts, but we do read them and our excellent Player Experience team is constantly in touch with you all to keep us in check. We knew that the release of Engineering would be a challenge and that due to the amount of the changes we've introduced it can be even trickier to get things right. Some of the balance changes we did early in this PTU cycle have been temporarily reverted to ensure we have a more stable base to balance and eliminate factors that could cause unforseen edge cases. As mentioned during the recent ISC, Engineering Gameplay is here to stay and we will do our best to work with you all and make it the best it can be. Cheers,

title: Re: AMD GI-1.2
summary: Quite annoyingly, "nanite-style" continuous-level-of-detail stuff pulls in the opposite direction from what current-gen ray-tracing APIs want you to do. With continuous-LOD, sections of objects are constantly swapping in and out, while the ray-tracing API wants you to generate whole-object acceleration structures that you don't change too often, so the two are kind of enemies. This also gives us challenges with ray-tracing and dynamic destruction, for similar reasons.

Once we have a good foundation and we are happy enough with it, we will start looking into all the things we tried out in the past. To be honest here, some of those past ideas might not stand the test of time so some things we thought might be good in the past might be replaced with better solutions.  Our intention is once we have all the base functionality for engineering working, we will investigate further and communicate to all of you what and how we will expand the feature. Once we are back in the next year I will hopefully be able to provide some information on the plans for Engineering in 2026. Right now we are still busy improving the balance of what we have in 4.5.  Cheers,

title: Re: No answer on my Request
summary: Hello! Larger game companies tend to have pretty specialized roles. Most of the devs that respond to questions here don't have access to our customer service tools and wouldn't be able to read the request. I used to have access to them, but that was something like 11 years ago back when we were smaller and I was doing a combination of QA and tech support work.  Without additional information, I wouldn't be able to comment on if the issue is a bug or a tech support issue so I don't want to rule out either of them. Especially since we just released a new patch and that's when we tend to see most account breaking bugs happen. To know for sure which of the two it might be, I'd need more information. For example: If it's a client crash, I'd need the digest ID which would allow me to look up which crash someone is running into. If it's a disconnection error, I'd need to know what the error number is. If it's something else like an infinite loading screen, that information is useful as well.   If it ends up not being an issue with the game, as a few people here have mentioned, the help desk is a good place to go for assistance. If you prefer forums instead of chat, we also have our community tech support forum where there are a lot of regulars that help people navigate various issues and get them back to playing. At this point, they're much better at it than I am because I haven't done any dedicated tech support work for years.

Especially since we just released a new patch and that's when we tend to see most account breaking bugs happen. To know for sure which of the two it might be, I'd need more information. For example: If it's a client crash, I'd need the digest ID which would allow me to look up which crash someone is running into. If it's a disconnection error, I'd need to know what the error number is. If it's something else like an infinite loading screen, that information is useful as well. If it ends up not being an issue with the game, as a few people here have mentioned, the help desk is a good place to go for assistance. If you prefer forums instead of chat, we also have our community tech support forum where there are a lot of regulars that help people navigate various issues and get them back to playing. At this point, they're much better at it than I am because I haven't done any dedicated tech support work for years.

title: Star Citizen Graphics Settings
summary: Hi everyone,  I wanted to take a moment to help clarify what each of our Graphics Settings does and how they impact your experience. Below, you’ll find a brief description of each setting, along with notes on what it affects in terms of performance, visuals, or hardware usage.  If you have any questions, feel free to ask below. I’ll do my best to jump in and answer where I can.  Video Memory (VRAM) The horizontal bar in the bottom right of the Graphics Options menu shows the maximum video memory the game will use with the chosen resolution + settings. It is crucial this is kept below the recommended maximum, but if you are running other software (e.g. recording/streaming) then you may need to leave more headroom. If you run out of VRAM, especially on Vulkan, then you will see huge performance dips (e.g. going from 60fps to 10fps) and this won’t recover until the memory goes back under the limit. Actual usage can vary throughout the game, based on locations and other players.  Setting Descriptions  Graphics Renderer [Desc] Changes the graphics API used for rendering (Vulkan/DX11) [Affects] Vulkan is the more modern API, and will be mandated in a future patch as it supports the latest hardware features such as ray tracing, whereas DX11 is no longer being updated Vulkan graphics drivers tend to change more frequently, and so are at more risk of bugs, so we always recommend being on the latest ‘safe’ driver, and avoid experimental drivers. If you hit issues after a driver update then roll back to the most recent working driver. If you have issues running Vulkan on any driver then we strongly recommend you report them so that you are not blocked from running the game in a future patch CPU performance should be much better on Vulkan GPU performance should be broadly similar between APIs Visual quality should be identical on both Behaviour/support for driver related overrides such as frame-generation/motion smoothing may vary between graphics APIs, and is largely beyond CIG’s control. We recommend not using any such driver overrides or render-overlays if you experience any issues  Resolution [Desc] Sets the final output resolution (after any up-scaling). [Affects] Large impact on VRAM usage and GPU performance. Recommend 1080p for low-spec, and 4k only for more recent GPUs  Window Mode [Desc] Full screen vs windowed [Affects] GPU performance should be slightly better in full-screen, though using a higher resolution will counteract that  VSync [Desc] Enable or disable v-sync. Locks image updates to your monitors refresh rate, which also locks your frame-rate to a divisor of your refresh rate (e.g. 120/60/30/20 fps). When disabled you may see ‘screen tear’ where you see partial image updates. We recommend you set your monitor refresh rate via the OS to the maximum and then enable VSync [Affects] Screen tear. Frame-rate clamping.  Upscaling [Desc] Use a lower resolution internal resolution for some of the rendering (UI is not affected), and use temporal upscaling to recover that detail over time [Affects] Lower resolutions can drastically improve GPU performance, and can save VRAM  Upscaling Technique [Desc] Change the upscaling technique used. If you have an NVidia card then we recommend DLSS, and for all others we recommend CIG-TSR [Affects] Each technique has a different cost in VRAM and performance  Upscaling Model ( DLSS only ) [Desc] Different variants of NVidia’s DLSS upscaling [Affects] Can be a large performance difference between modes  HDR [Desc] Enable High Dynamic Range output for improved contrast [Affects] Performance should be near identical. This can have an impact on screenshots and your ability to stream content  HDR Brightness (Ref-White) ( HDR only ) [Desc] Desired brightness of a comfortable ‘paper white'. Adjust based on the light levels in your room. Ideally HDR is experienced in a dim room with a low reference white setting to maximize the contrast of bright highlights. Typical values are between 100 and 300, but vary massively depending on your monitor and viewing conditions. [Affects] Typical brightness of a white object/screen.  HDR Peak Brightness ( HDR only ) [Desc] Maximum brightness to use. Recommended setting is the maximum, which is automatically detected from your display, and only lower if uncomfortable. [Affects] Maximum brightness of lights & reflections  Overall Quality Preset [Desc] Sets all quality controls below to the same setting [Affects] VRAM, GPU performance & quality (see below for details) Object Detail [Desc] Adjusts polygon detail on meshes via changing the distances that each ‘level of detail’ is used, and whether to use hardware tessellation (High and above) [Affects] GPU performance  Object View Distance [Desc] Controls the maximum distance at which objects are drawn (up to 200% difference between Ultra and Low) [Affects] GPU performance and minor CPU cost  Textures Quality [Desc] Changes the amount of VRAM used for streaming textures, as well as the target resolution of textures [Values] Ultra = 5800Mb, Very High = 4300Mb, High = 3300Mb, Medium = 2300Mb with 25% quality reduction, Low = 1400Mb with 50% quality reduction [Affects] VRAM, and increased disk access at higher settings Detail Textures [Desc] Changes the resolution of textures used for details on characters, weapons and items/props. [Values] High = 512x512, Medium = 256x256, Low = 128x128 [Affects] VRAM Ground Textures [Desc] Sets the resolution of ground textures used on planets [Values] High = 2048x2048, Low = 1024x1024 [Affects] VRAM Texture Filtering [Desc] Sets anisotropic texture filtering quality for preserving details at grazing angles [Values] High = 16x, Medium = 8x, Low = 4x [Affects] GPU performance Shadow Maps [Desc] Changes the resolution of shadow maps as well as their quality. [Values] Ultra = 200%, Very High/High = 100%, Medium/Low = 50% [Affects] VRAM & GPU performance

title: Re: Vulkan Questions
summary: I don't have a specific answer for why it doesn't work as yet. However usually these driver level features intercept the game's render commands and inject their own commands to try and add new behaviour, so they're largely outside of our control. DX11 and Vulkan have different drivers, and we also have different approaches to synchronizing the frame to the driver/display, so the feature working on one graphics API has no real bearing on the other.
body_html: I don't have a specific answer for why it doesn't work as yet. However usually these driver level features intercept the game's render commands and inject their own commands to try and add new behaviour, so they're largely outside of our control. DX11 and Vulkan have different drivers, and we also have different approaches to synchronizing the frame to the driver/display, so the feature working on one graphics API has no real bearing on the other.

title: Re: Star Citizen Graphics Settings
summary: Screenspace Shadows [Desc] Changes the rendering quality settings of screenspace shadows [Affects] Visual quality & GPU performance  Planet Volumetric Clouds Quality [Desc] Changes the rendering quality settings of planet clouds [Affects] Visual quality & GPU performance  Gas Clouds [Desc] Changes the rendering quality settings of gas (space) clouds [Affects] Visual quality & GPU performance  Fog [Desc] Changes the resolution of the local fog (i.e. fog within 500m). Higher settings will preserve more detail in shafts of light, lower values will have a flatter appearance.  [Affects] Visual quality, VRAM & GPU performance  Water Caustics [Desc] Enables water caustics effects (light scattered onto objects beneath the water) [Affects] GPU performance  Water Simulation [Desc] Controls the number of simultaneous water simulations that can occur at once [Affects] VRAM & GPU performance  Shader Quality [Desc] Adjusts the quality of some material shader effects, such as parallax occlusion mapping (to add 3D details to otherwise flat surfaces). [Affects] Visual quality & GPU performance  Post Effects [Desc] Controls the quality of some post effects such as Motion Blur, Bloom, Flares & Refraction [Affects] GPU performance  Video Comms [Desc] Controls the quality of lighting in video comms calls [Affects] GPU performance  Visor and Lens Aspect Modifier [Desc] Aspect ratio for the UI displayed on the visor/lens. Useful for ultra wide monitors or multi-monitor setups. [Affects] Visual only  Field Of View [Desc] Horizontal field of view.  [Affects] Can affect both CPU and GPU performance  Gamma [Desc] Adjusts the midtone brightness curve without changing pure black or white levels. Increase if dark areas appear too dark, decrease if the image looks washed out. [Affects] Visual only  Brightness [Desc] Controls the overall brightness level of the image. Adjust so that dark scenes are visible but blacks remain true black. [Affects] Visual only  Contrast [Desc] Adjusts the difference between the darkest and brightest parts of the image. Higher values create more dramatic differences between light and dark areas. [Affects] Visual only  Motion Blur [Desc] Enables/disables motion blur. Camera rotation does just apply very little blur to mimic saccadic masking and improve clarity, meaning blur should mostly occur with camera translation or object movement. Shutter speed is equivalent to a 60 fps camera with the shutter open half the frame. [Affects] GPU performance & image clarity when moving  Sharpening [Desc] Applies post-process sharpening to enhance edge definition and perceived detail. Can help counteract softness from upscaling techniques but may introduce artifacts if set too high. [Affects] Visuals only  Chromatic Aberration [Desc] Simulates lens color fringing effect seen in real cameras. Adds a 'filmic' look but can be disabled for greater clarity. [Affects] Visuals only  Film Grain [Desc] Adds a subtle grain texture overlay to simulate analog film cameras. Purely aesthetic effect that can be disabled for greater clarity.  [Affects] Visuals only

title: Re: Star Citizen Graphics Settings
summary: As the others say, you are likely running out of VRAM.   The next bit is a bit techy, so feel free to ignore (but I'm sure some will find it interesting):  To verify if you are hitting the memory issue you can open the console and type r_displayInfo 4, and look for the line with "VRAM(MB): A / B", where A is what is being used by Star Citizen and B is the budget (though this doesn't account for other applications that may also be using VRAM).   Also if you see the line "VRAM Demoted: C, OSBudget: D MB" then you are likely suffering the major performance issue I mention, where C is the amount of VRAM that has been transferred to RAM (CPU memory) but is really needed on the GPU, and D is the VRAM budget the the OS would like the game to run within (which factors in other applications).

summary: If you’re CPU bound then unfortunately none of the graphics options will really help (though Vulkan and lowering Objetc View Distance may help a bit).   CPU usage will vary hugely with location and other players and their ships. Perhaps try joining the same server in the same location to compare.   if their GPU/resolution/settings are  lower then they may be GPU bound with a lower frame rate, which will then free up their CPU and make it look less busy.   I’ve said it a few times on this forum, but overall usage % for both CPU and GPU are not great indicators and are very easy to misinterpret. Instead just determine if you are CPU or GPU bound (r.ProfileGraph 1 can help here), and only focus on what can be done to alleviate that. Everything else is largely irrelevant.

title: Re: Star Citizen Graphics Settings
summary: Frame pacing is a hugely complex topic, so I wont dive too deep here in this thread.   But it’s highly subjective, and we can’t please everyone. For many, 50fps on a 60Hz monitor feels juddery, because the game can’t predict which frames will take too long, so they’re all simulated as the same amount of time. This is a problem because while an object may be moving N meters per T milliseconds, on the frame that is “dropped” the object will move N meters in 2T milliseconds (because we see this frame twice), ie it’ll temporally be half the speed. So for many, 30fps is preferable when dropping below 60fps. Of course it’s much better to have a higher refresh display and also freesync, as then you can achieve smooth framerates beyond just 30 and 60.   It’s also worth mentioning that we measure the previous frame time, and intentionally smooth the frame rate over time, so we shouldn’t bounce between 60 and 30 too frequently.

title: Re: Star Citizen Graphics Settings
summary: The “VRAM Demoted” thing isn’t always a problem. We allocate memory in large chunks, typically around 250mb, and over time we shift memory between these chunks to use as few as possible. If the driver finds a chunk that isn’t being used (eg we reserve some mem for planets but it’s not used in outer space) then it may demote it to RAM without any performance impact. However when you run out of VRAM it’ll demote stuff that IS being used, and this means it needs to reupload to GPU and then immediately discard many of these chunks every single frame.. which is catastrophic For performance.   Btw we’d get identical behaviour on DX12, so those calling for this as a solution wouldn’t be saved. We’ve got some tech in progress which allows better re-use of the same VRAM via multiple systems, and should lower our peak VRAM requirement to help those experiencing issues.   For those with 6Gb or 8GB if it helps to run DX11 that’s fine (and should be improved by the above), but what we really need to diagnose is the issues stopping people running Vulkan at all.

title: Re: Honestly, where is the new flight model CIG? Can we get an answer on if it's coming in 2026?
summary: Heya, we can't answer "when" questions but I can give a bit of context.  The FM feature work for S42 is completed (IFCS, control surfaces, quantum, carrier ops, etc.) and we're just doing smaller follow-up work (e.g. code clean-up, tuning, minor bug fixes, UI adjustments, etc.). The same underlying tech is already in the PU dev streams.  But while S42 is relatively straight forward to tune and balance, it has a much smaller ship roster and as a single player game we have greater control over the experience. The PU with it's PVP parts is a different beast. We have hundreds of ships and variants and every single one needs the flight model retuned for NFM and made sure it sits in the right spot.  During the MM update we had to update the flight model of all ships within a single release cycle because the technology didn't support parallel flight models. That was very demanding on us devs and initially didn't allow us to focus on the unique characteristics of each ship. The new tech now supports parallel NFM models which means we can take our time with each ship as the legacy FM data is still intact.  And that's why we're taking a more granular approach this time: Instead of a large, sweeping change, we're gradually going through every ship and setup its individual character from the outset. That involves extensive validation through focused playtesting, iteration, rinse, repeat and that process has been going on for a while now.  I am actually super happy with the progress but we do not have yet enough ships converted to start public testing. We'll show things when we will feel it's ready.  I hope that clears it up a bit.  TLDR: Progress is really good but not ready to show yet.

In an ideal world I'd do a different recoil for VR users to sell the weapons a lot more as when I've used them it feels really flat because it's all built for centre of camera.

title: Re: Super Ultra Wide Stretching
summary: Your summoning has been heard!  This comes up once in a while from people. This can only be fixed with multiple projections and renderpasses which some games like MSFS support. This would require a huge and immense effort and rewrite from our side of large parts of the engine and is not planned at the moment. As others were saying the only way to minimize this effect is to reduce the FOV. This is just how perspective projections work. If this bothers you too much i recommend to reduce the aspect ratio, so you have black bars on left and right.
body_html: Your summoning has been heard! This comes up once in a while from people. This can only be fixed with multiple projections and renderpasses which some games like MSFS support. This would require a huge and immense effort and rewrite from our side of large parts of the engine and is not planned at the moment. As others were saying the only way to minimize this effect is to reduce the FOV. This is just how perspective projections work. If this bothers you too much i recommend to reduce the aspect ratio, so you have black bars on left and right.

title: Pricing Surge
summary: Today we are introducing Pricing Surge, a new time limited in-game activity.  As we move through 2026, Star Citizen is evolving not just in what we deliver, but in how we deliver it. Alongside upcoming changes to patch scheduling that we will talk about in more detail soon, we are also starting to roll out smaller, targeted pieces of content that can go live without waiting for a full patch.  Pricing Surge is the first of these. The goal is to create short term, high impact opportunities in the live universe that react to what is happening in the verse, give players new ways to engage, and let us adjust and iterate faster based on how you play. What is Pricing Surge? Taking advantage of a glut of salvaged Atlasium in the wake of an unusually high number of capital ship battles, a few clever vendors in the Stanton system have cornered the market of the rare material, selling it at premium price.   For those of you without the aUEC at hand, the vendors are also offering higher-than-average prices on a few other commodities that they're eager to get their hands on.  Devlin Scrap & Salvage: Amioshi Plague Altruciatoxin Pitambu  Brio's Breaker Yard: Thermal Foam Tungsten  Profit-seeking traders are encouraged to seek out and discover these prosperous vendors in the ‘verse, but beware that quantities are limited, and others may be seeking these fortunes in less-than-friendly ways.  This demand is temporary and will fade once their needs are met and the market stabilizes with the next major update, Alpha 4.6.  Fly dangerously safe!

Devlin Scrap & Salvage: Amioshi Plague Altruciatoxin Pitambu Brio's Breaker Yard: Thermal Foam Tungsten Profit-seeking traders are encouraged to seek out and discover these prosperous vendors in the ‘verse, but beware that quantities are limited, and others may be seeking these fortunes in less-than-friendly ways. This demand is temporary and will fade once their needs are met and the market stabilizes with the next major update, Alpha 4.6. Fly dangerously safe!

title: Roadmap Roundup - January 14, 2026
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.  With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!  -CIG Community Team Release View 4.6.0  Cockpit Light Amplification (LAMP) Implementing light amplification on the canopies of a limited set of vehicles, allowing players to more easily navigate the 'verse in low-light conditions, with more ships to be supported in the future. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Clearing The Air Implementing a system wide crisis on Levski built around the Molina Mold outbreak, sending players across Nyx and Stanton on Hauling, Courier, Resource Gathering, Kill Ship, Recover Cargo, Station Escort, and Defend Ship missions. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  New Resource Gathering Missions Implementing an expanded list of missions to our Resource Gathering archetype. Find, gather and deliver raw or refined mineable ores or salvageable ship pieces for a variety of corporations. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Kel-To Ship Supply Kiosks Implementing small, Kel-To owned ship supply kiosks at major cities in Stanton, giving crews quick access to engineering tools and essential provisions. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  FPS Weapons Art Refactor Updating visual material and texture for the following weapons and equipments: Behring P4-AR, FS-9, and P6-LR; Greycat MaxLift Tractor Beam and Cambio SRT; CureLife ParaMed Medical Device; and Ripper SMG. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.

title: Re: About bullpup rifles
summary: Speaking only from an animation stand point this would be tricky, but not impossible. For our 2-handed weapons, I believe the distance from the end of the stock to the pistol grip is the same across all the weapons. This allows us to share animations. The only change is the left hand and where it grips the upper receiver.  A bullpup weapon changes this arrangement, so we would have to figure out what the downstream impacts of that would be. They could be significant.

title: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (4.6 Updates)
summary: Hey everyone,  We hope you’ve been enjoying the native Experimental VR support we introduced over during the holidays in Alpha 4.5. The response has been absolutely mind-blowing, and seeing it in your hands and the joy it’s bringing has been incredibly rewarding for the team.  Naturally, there is still a lot of work to do to make it what it’s meant to be. With that in mind, here are the changes we’ve prepared for Alpha 4.6, along with a few additional developer comments from my side:   Bug Fixes & Stability Fixed a bunch of crashes, especially when turning VR on. Also added better error descriptions with suggestions for common issues (e.g., uninstalling OpenXR Tools, which does cause issues at the moment). Fixed FOG not affecting transparent objects, especially visible on microTech when caught in a snowstorm. Fixed CameraViewLookBehind not applying HMD tracking. No longer apply the IPD scale to head tracking movements if it's below 1.0f. This caused head movements to slow as you lowered the IPD scale. No longer reset the head tracking in any kind of interaction mode in FPS. This fixes the issue where people wouldn't get close enough to a terminal to read it.   New Options Selection for FPS ADS offset to the dominant eye. Extended Mirror Mode - More on that down below. Stereo Cursor Scale, Sensitivity, and Coupling to Head Movement. Eye tracking support for the stereo cursor. Depth of field toggle. MobiGlas Distance.   Stereo Cursor Improvements Implemented stereo cursor decoupling from the head motion. This is also the default option now and should feel more natural. Note that the stereo cursor has a range and is anchored to a specific pixel position when it is activated. This can be changed in the settings.   Eye Tracking Support A small experiment on my part, as I was curious to see how well it would work. I've tried it only with the Pimax Crystal Super, and although it was good enough, it wasn't perfect. Proper calibration is very important.  You can customize the behavior with these 4 cvars: r_StereoEyeTrackingSmoothing r_StereoEyeTrackingDeadzone r_StereoEyeTrackingCalibrationX r_StereoEyeTrackingCalibrationY   Mirror Mode Update r_StereoScreenOutput renamed to r_StereoMirrorMode Added both left & right eye variants for Fill and aspect ratio maintaining Added smoothing, zoom and pan functionality. Can be customized via r_StereoMirrorModeZoom, r_StereoMirrorModeSmoothing, r_StereoMirrorModePanX/Y The smoothing at the moment is a simple roll stabilization, similar to what Half-Life Alyx does. To do that, the view needs to be zoomed in; otherwise, you will get black borders. Note that the fill modes also zoom in more than they did previously as they try to center the view now. You can always manually use the cvars for any custom setups if you want. I'm still not super happy with the Mirror Modes, but hopefully that should make it a little bit better for the time being. Ultimately, the best viewing experience is only given with a separate camera. This renders an entirely separate view, which is very expensive. I think we should be able to leverage the RTT system to render a separate camera, with limited capabilities, however. No ETA when this will come.   Theater Mode Added theater mode screen curvature support using XR_KHR_composition_layer_cylinder This is, unfortunately, a very limited supported extension (SteamVR and Pimax don't support it, but Meta does). This was just a temporary test and will be replaced by a custom solution in the future with many more features.  What I would like to see: Ambient lighting, 3D Mode, Different Environments (different skybox depending on where you are in the universe!), and more!   Launcher Update The Launcher will soon get an update to enable/disable VR! This is needed so that SteamVR doesn't launch automatically anymore for some headsets when VR isn't desired.  This is off by default, so once the launcher update comes, you need to turn on VR explicitly.   What's Next? The Marker/UI rework is still a work in progress. I can't promise that we will be able to fix it for 4.6, but we are trying!  Many people have already figured out that you can use r_StereoUILensDepth and CV_r_StereoScaleformDepth to fix it. However, that breaks other stuff. Feel free to experiment with it and find something that works for you.   Edit 19/01/26: - Fixed smurf mode (inverted colors) in VR on Linux - Removed all UI/Visor shakes in VR - Add new option for Direct Offset control when targeting (ADS). This only does something if the Actor Control Mode is set to Grounded Look (stable image)  Edit 22/01/26: - Fixed a crash that occurred when enabling HDR with a connected headset. HDR is now automatically disabled when VR is enabled to prevent display issues. Added true HDR support for VR as well. Can be enabled with r_StereoModeAllowHDR=1. This requires an HDR Monitor too. Note that using HDR for VR doesn't make any sense and will look wrong if the headset itself does not support HDR. - Disabled motion compensation layer by default to prevent crashes (toggle with sys_openxr_layer_disable_motion_compensation=0 in user.cfg) - Disabled OpenXR Toolkit by default due to compatibility issues (toggle with sys_openxr_layer_disable_openxr_toolkit=0 in user.cfg) - The UI menue is now world-locked in front of the player instead of view-aligned. This significantly improves usability, especially for lower resolution headsets. The old behavior can still be restored with CV_r_StereoUIAttachedToView=1  Edit 06/03/26: The native Pimax OpenXR is no longer blocked by EAC and can be freely used now.  That's it for now! I will catch you in the 'verse (and hopefully in VR!) :blush:  - Silvan

The old behavior can still be restored with CV_r_StereoUIAttachedToView=1 Edit 06/03/26: The native Pimax OpenXR is no longer blocked by EAC and can be freely used now. That's it for now! I will catch you in the 'verse (and hopefully in VR!) :blush: - Silvan

title: Re: [4.6.0 PTU Feedback] Industrial Salvage and Mining Missions
summary: Just a high level note, cause i've been reading it a lot.  As many have guessed, but some not. The Balancing is not Final, its not even implemented, the amount of contracts we had to make means the data is the base inherited one without any tweaks at all. The Econ team is working on the balancing and you will see it come online very very soon. To go further into this by balancing I mean Amount you get paid and the Amount to Deliver.  As for some of the flow issues you notice (e.g. Getting loads of gems in a box and submitting that) we are aware of it.  No missions just asking for Raw Ore we cant support that currently, but its wanted and we are working on it, just didn't make this release. And some of the others  Have fun bobs! Me and my Vulture/Prospector are gonna get a TON of use

summary: The scopes and sights don't work properly in VR yet. The issue is known but I don't know when it will be fixed. It's not a VR specific problem either, the same issues will pop up using normal headtracking but because the offseting limits are a bit stricter they usually are not as apparent.
body_html: The scopes and sights don't work properly in VR yet. The issue is known but I don't know when it will be fixed. It's not a VR specific problem either, the same issues will pop up using normal headtracking but because the offseting limits are a bit stricter they usually are not as apparent.

title: Re: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (4.6 Updates)
summary: PIPs and crosshair size will not get a VR specific option. They have a fixed angle size but we'd rather extend the MFD configuration settings to cover more than just "on / off" switches so that the size can be freely scaled and all players can benefit from it.
body_html: PIPs and crosshair size will not get a VR specific option. They have a fixed angle size but we'd rather extend the MFD configuration settings to cover more than just "on / off" switches so that the size can be freely scaled and all players can benefit from it.

title: Re: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (4.6 Updates)
summary: I'm waiting for an eye tracking capable headset to arrive, when it's here we'll check whether we allow actual gimbal aiming via eyes. I am not sold on it yet as it may cause an unfair advantage in space combat ... we already allow slaving the gimbals to your view direction in VR and in certain situations it is already pretty powerful.
body_html: I'm waiting for an eye tracking capable headset to arrive, when it's here we'll check whether we allow actual gimbal aiming via eyes. I am not sold on it yet as it may cause an unfair advantage in space combat ... we already allow slaving the gimbals to your view direction in VR and in certain situations it is already pretty powerful.

title: Re: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (4.6 Updates)
summary: Hello everyone! We've got some more updates on the way. They will appear in one of the next builds likely tomorrow.  HDR Compatibility Fixed a crash that occurred when enabling HDR with a connected headset. HDR is now automatically disabled when VR is enabled to prevent display issues. However, while I was at it, i've added true HDR support for VR as well. It can be enabled with r_StereoModeAllowHDR=1. This requires an HDR Monitor too. Note that there are not many headsets with HDR on the market and if you turn it on with a non-hdr capable headset colors will look very wrong. Regardless, the future will be bright for Star Citizen VR :slightly_smiling_face:  OpenXR Layer Management Disabled motion compensation layer by default to prevent crashes (toggle with sys_openxr_layer_disable_motion_compensation=0 in user.cfg) Disabled OpenXR Toolkit by default due to compatibility issues (toggle with sys_openxr_layer_disable_openxr_toolkit=0 in user.cfg)  Menu System The UI menue is now world-locked in front of the player instead of view-aligned. This significantly improves usability, especially for lower resolution headsets. The old behavior can still be restored with CV_r_StereoUIAttachedToView=1
body_html: Hello everyone! We've got some more updates on the way. They will appear in one of the next builds likely tomorrow. HDR Compatibility Fixed a crash that occurred when enabling HDR with a connected headset. HDR is now automatically disabled when VR is enabled to prevent display issues. However, while I was at it, i've added true HDR support for VR as well. It can be enabled with r_StereoModeAllowHDR=1. This requires an HDR Monitor too. Note that there are not many headsets with HDR on the market and if you turn it on with a non-hdr capable headset colors will look very wrong. Regardless, the future will be bright for Star Citizen VR :slightly_smiling_face: OpenXR Layer Management Disabled motion compensation layer by default to prevent crashes (toggle with sys_openxr_layer_disable_motion_compensation=0 in user.cfg) Disabled OpenXR Toolkit by default due to compatibility issues (toggle with sys_openxr_layer_disable_openxr_toolkit=0 in user.cfg) Menu System The UI menue is now world-locked in front of the player instead of view-aligned. This significantly improves usability, especially for lower resolution headsets. The old behavior can still be restored with CV_r_StereoUIAttachedToView=1

title: Alpha 4.6 - Lifeline for Levski
summary: Hi everyone,  A fast-spreading contamination has pushed Levski into a full-scale emergency, with failing air systems and a growing number of civilians falling ill. What began as a localized issue has now become a system-wide crisis, drawing attention and resources from across Nyx and Stanton!  You are being called in to move critical supplies, investigate the source of the outbreak, protect vulnerable operations, and keep trade and travel flowing under this outbreak. From hauling and courier work to combat and escort missions, every mission you complete helps stabilize Levski and push the crisis toward resolution. The population of Levski counts you, citizens!  Alongside Clearing The Air, Alpha 4.6: Lifeline for Levski delivers a wide range of new and updated gameplay. Industrial Resource Gathering missions expand mining, salvaging, refining, and scavenging into faction-driven contracts that send you across Stanton, Pyro, and Nyx (Coming in a .x patch). Cockpits now support the new LAMP light amplification system, improving visibility in low-light conditions for a growing list of ships. This release also brings the RSI Aurora Mk I to gold standard, significant VR improvements, new inventory options for Pyro rest-stop black markets, new supplies shops at major landing zones in Stanton, ground vehicle missile balance passes, and ongoing ship and weapon updates, and more! Star Citizen Alpha 4.6: Lifeline for Levski is now available. Ready your hazard suit, the Molina mold is highly toxic. title: FAQ - Clearing The Air
summary: Clearing The Air arrives in the Persistent Universe as a system-wide crisis centered on Levski, Nyx. What began as a wave of unexplained illness, now known as the People’s Ailment, has escalated into a full emergency spreading across Nyx and Stanton. The source has been traced back to a dangerous new mold strain growing in faulty air filters supplied by Gyson Inc, discovered after the death of maintenance engineer Samuel Molina.  As you push back the outbreak and support the effort to stabilize Levski, completing missions will unlock milestone activities that mark major progress in the crisis. Whether you are flying support, moving critical supplies, or taking the fight directly to hostile forces, every job plays a role in Clearing The Air: There is something for everyone! We’ve put together answers to your most common questions about the event. ▲ What is the "Clearing The Air" event? Clearing The Air is a limited-time event running from January 28 to March 17, 2026, responding to a health crisis in Levski.  A deadly fungal infection known as the "Molina Mold" has been spreading through the station due to faulty air filters, causing a disease called the People's Ailment with symptoms including coughing, fatigue, chest pain, and bone lesions. With the death toll rising into double digits and spreading to the Stanton system, the UEE has mobilized contractors to help contain the outbreak.  You'll participate in relief efforts by transporting medical supplies, delivering antifungal treatments, gathering resources to manufacture replacement filters and cures, and defending supply convoys from criminal gangs like the Moraine, who are exploiting the crisis. The event features multiple mission types across Transport, Defense, and Collection divisions, with all phases available from day one.  Your contributions will earn points toward both the overall goal and division-specific rewards.    ▲ How can I accept the new mission? Clearing The Air missions are available through your mobiGlas's contracts, and multiple mission providers are organized into three divisions:  Transport Division - Accept hauling and courier contracts from: Ling Family Hauling for mold treatments Covalex and FTL Courier for cryopods, ventilation filters, medical supplies, and samples Collection Division - Find resource gathering missions from the corporations to manufacture filters and cures: Shubin Interstellar from Hurston Rayari Inc from microTech Defense Division - Take combat contracts from: Eckhart for eliminating Moraine gang targets and recovering stolen cargo Citizens For Prosperity for escort and ship defense missions, protecting relief supply convoys  As you complete missions within each division, you'll unlock special milestone activities after reaching certain thresholds.    ▲ Can I participate in multiple divisions, or do I need to choose one? You can participate in all three divisions (Transport, Defense, and Collection) and earn rewards from each! Your mission completion counts toward both the overall progress and your divisions' progress.    ▲ What are Milestone activities, and how do I unlock them? Milestone activities are special, hard difficulty missions that citizens can access once enough progress has been made in individual divisions.  These missions are only playable once, boosting your progress and delivering more unique narrative scenarios: Transport: Pick up critical commodities needed to address the situation in Levski. Collection: Source and deliver commodities to support the initiative, and help find a solution to the Molina Mold. Defense: Protect the Alliance Aid ships against the Moraine gang in Nyx, then transport their valuable cargo back to Stanton for study. ▲ What kind of rewards can I earn? Rewards are earned by accumulating points through mission completion, tracked across both overall progress and individual divisions:  Overall Rewards: 30% - CureLife Light Medical Armor + MaxLift AA Support Tractor Beam 70% - Asgard Ship Paint 90% - Apollo Medivac Ship Paint 100% - Perseus Ship Paint + ParaMed "AA Support" Medical Device + Item Fabricator RediMake "Alliance Aid" Note: The Item Fabricator RediMake “Alliance Aid” will only be available once the Crafting feature releases in a future patch. This skin showcases the efforts you made during the Clearing the Air event, and its final design may vary as a work in progress item.  Quick update on our previous note: As you know, the first iteration of Crafting will be launching with Alpha 4.7, but the Item Fabricator RediMake "Alliance Aid" skin will be coming in Alpha 4.8.   Transport Division Rewards: 10% - Transport Division Jacket 50% - MaxLift 'Transport' Skin 100% - RAFT Ship Paint Defense Division Rewards: 10% - Defense Division Jacket 50% - Ship Weapon skin (BEHR Laser Cannon S1-3) 100% - Paladin Ship Paint Collection Division Rewards: 10% - Collection Division Jacket 50% - Purifier Mask AA Support 100% - Apollo Triage Ship Paint ▲ Where does this event take place? You'll be traveling between multiple systems to deliver supplies, with most relief efforts coordinating from Stanton to help the affected population in Levski, Nyx.  You can accept the event's missions from anywhere.    ▲ Do I need a specific ship or equipment to participate? No specific ship is required! The event offers many missions across different scales and playstyles: Small-grade missions, for starter ships and solo players mostly Medium and supply-grade missions, for mid-size ships Bulk-grade missions, for large haulers and teams specifically organized (Or very determined individuals!) Combat missions are scaled to easy, medium, and hard difficulties. Choose missions that match your ship's capabilities and your preferred gameplay style.    ▲ Who are The Moraine, and why are they involved? The Moraine is a loyal syndicate of thieves and smugglers that operates a highly profitable smuggling ring across Nyx's many jump points. Since a weakened People's Alliance would only strengthen their own hold on the system, they're eager to exploit the Molina Mold crisis by hijacking delivery ships carrying medical supplies and filters, and holding mold-infected victims in cryopods for ransom.   Alliance Aid Defense Division contracts specifically counter these criminal activities by protecting convoys, eliminating gang targets, and recovering stolen supplies before more lives are lost.

Clearing The Air missions are available through your mobiGlas's contracts, and multiple mission providers are organized into three divisions: Transport Division - Accept hauling and courier contracts from: Ling Family Hauling for mold treatments Covalex and FTL Courier for cryopods, ventilation filters, medical supplies, and samples Collection Division - Find resource gathering missions from the corporations to manufacture filters and cures: Shubin Interstellar from Hurston Rayari Inc from microTech Defense Division - Take combat contracts from: Eckhart for eliminating Moraine gang targets and recovering stolen cargo Citizens For Prosperity for escort and ship defense missions, protecting relief supply convoys As you complete missions within each division, you'll unlock special milestone activities after reaching certain thresholds. ▲ Can I participate in multiple divisions, or do I need to choose one? You can participate in all three divisions (Transport, Defense, and Collection) and earn rewards from each! Your mission completion counts toward both the overall progress and your divisions' progress. ▲ What are Milestone activities, and how do I unlock them? Milestone activities are special, hard difficulty missions that citizens can access once enough progress has been made in individual divisions. These missions are only playable once, boosting your progress and delivering more unique narrative scenarios: Transport: Pick up critical commodities needed to address the situation in Levski. Collection: Source and deliver commodities to support the initiative, and help find a solution to the Molina Mold. Defense: Protect the Alliance Aid ships against the Moraine gang in Nyx, then transport their valuable cargo back to Stanton for study. ▲ What kind of rewards can I earn? Rewards are earned by accumulating points through mission completion, tracked across both overall progress and individual divisions: Overall Rewards: 30% - CureLife Light Medical Armor + MaxLift AA Support Tractor Beam 70% - Asgard Ship Paint 90% - Apollo Medivac Ship Paint 100% - Perseus Ship Paint + ParaMed "AA Support" Medical Device + Item Fabricator RediMake "Alliance Aid" Note: The Item Fabricator RediMake “Alliance Aid” will only be available once the Crafting feature releases in a future patch. This skin showcases the efforts you made during the Clearing the Air event, and its final design may vary as a work in progress item. Quick update on our previous note: As you know, the first iteration of Crafting will be launching with Alpha 4.7, but the Item Fabricator RediMake "Alliance Aid" skin will be coming in Alpha 4.8. Transport Division Rewards: 10% - Transport Division Jacket 50% - MaxLift 'Transport' Skin 100% - RAFT Ship Paint Defense Division Rewards: 10% - Defense Division Jacket 50% - Ship Weapon skin (BEHR Laser Cannon S1-3) 100% - Paladin Ship Paint Collection Division Rewards: 10% - Collection Division Jacket 50% - Purifier Mask AA Support 100% - Apollo Triage Ship Paint ▲ Where does this event take place? You'll be traveling between multiple systems to deliver supplies, with most relief efforts coordinating from Stanton to help the affected population in Levski, Nyx. You can accept the event's missions from anywhere. ▲ Do I need a specific ship or equipment to participate? No specific ship is required! The event offers many missions across different scales and playstyles: Small-grade missions, for starter ships and solo players mostly Medium and supply-grade missions, for mid-size ships Bulk-grade missions, for large haulers and teams specifically organized (Or very determined individuals!) Combat missions are scaled to easy, medium, and hard difficulties. Choose missions that match your ship's capabilities and your preferred gameplay style. ▲ Who are The Moraine, and why are they involved? The Moraine is a loyal syndicate of thieves and smugglers that operates a highly profitable smuggling ring across Nyx's many jump points. Since a weakened People's Alliance would only strengthen their own hold on the system, they're eager to exploit the Molina Mold crisis by hijacking delivery ships carrying medical supplies and filters, and holding mold-infected victims in cryopods for ransom. Alliance Aid Defense Division contracts specifically counter these criminal activities by protecting convoys, eliminating gang targets, and recovering stolen supplies before more lives are lost.

title: Re: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (4.6 Updates)
summary: Hmm, openxr has its own frame prediction (lookup xrWaitFrame). What this does is sync the engine with whenever openxr thinks the next frame may be ready. This can introduce large waiting times on the CPU before we predict the next headpose. This is entirely controlled by openxr so nothing I can control. My guess is that you changed some settings which affects this behavior.

title: Star Citizen Alpha 4.6 LIVE - Hotfix Central [Updated 3.5.2026]
summary: Hi Everyone!  Time again for another Hotfix Central thread to keep you all up to date on things going on outside of the normal patch cycle in SC Alpha 4.6 LIVE! This will be a living document of all the hotfixes applied to the current LIVE environment, along with dates as a timeline and when the HOTFIX channel is open and closed.  These posts will be locked down to comments as the updates will span the entire 4.6 cycle so please check out the issue council and testing chats for any information you would like to let us know about!   2.11.2026: 4.6 Content Drop - 11218823 4.6 LIVE has been updated with the first content drop in 2026. This includes the enabling of Industrial Missions and more!  Industrial Salvage and Mining Missions Industrial Resource Gathering missions introduce a new mission type where factions contract you to acquire specific resources through various industrial gameplay loops. Unlike cargo hauling where shipments are provided, these missions require you to locate and gather the requested materials yourself using mining, refining, salvaging, scavenging, gathering, and even pirating activities across the Stanton, Pyro, and Nyx systems.  Core Gameplay Accept contracts requesting specific resources from mission givers and deliver to the requested location through the freight elevator     Mining: Extract minerals and raw ores using FPS mining tools, ground vehicles (ROC), or mining ships (Prospector, MOLE)     Salvaging: Scrape hulls for RMC, disintegrate ship structures for rubble/parts, or scavenge vehicle components from wrecks     Refining: Process raw ores sand scraps into refined materials at refinery stations Mission Providers & Reputation     Shubin Interstellar: Specializes in mining and refining contracts. Build reputation to unlock more challenging mining missions with better rewards     Adagio Holdings: Focuses on salvage and construction material contracts. Progress through reputation ranks to access expert salvaging opportunities  Changes and Fixes Bugfix: Fixed ParaMed "AA Support" Medical Device healing much more efficiently than intended Bugfix: Fixed excessive wear effect on Greys Market Shiv interior cockpit glass Fixed multiple Client and Server crashes   Current 4.6 LIVE Status | 3.5.2026 https://status.robertsspaceindustries.com/ Status: Hotfix Channel Currently Closed Latest LIVE Client CL: 11377160 Latest LIVE DGS CL: 11244073 (11377160 canaried to limited shards for testing)  ► 3.5.2026: 11377160 Client is now on the LIVE environment with the DGS side propagating out. This hotfix resolves crashes with the latest Nvidia Drivers (Client), NPCs cowering around landing zones because of toy pistols (We are looking into a few other ways this can happen), streaming out locations causing inventory to disappear, and quantum travel routes resetting after setting route ► 2.26.2026: CL 11319298 - LIVE has been updated with further DGS/Client side hotfixes for clean air reward acquisition, Arena Commander authentication, and DGS performance fixes ► 2.24.2026: Client side Hotfix with some undisclosed fixes has been sent to the LIVE environment. ► 2.12.2026: Hotfix 11244073 - We are currently rolling out DGS/Hybrid hotfixes on LIVE for multiple issues including hangars getting stowed (STARC-178893), network desync caused by temperature net spam, and AI combat ships desync during combat and appears to be teleporting. ► 2.11.2026: Content Drop 11218823 ► 2.2.2026: DGS/Hybrid hotfix 11173070 has been applied to nearly all shards with a handful of stability fixes for hybrid and DGS crashes ► 1.30.2026: We have applied a fix to LIVE to fix PVP ships not going critical and exploding when enough damage is applied. We are also currently testing Hybrid hotfixes for stability. ► 1.29.2026: Hotfix targets and discussion have begun for the 4.6 cycle. Will update here as hotfixes become available.   Using the HOTFIX channel The HOTFIX channel will become available for periods of time when the client-side of the game needs the hotfix. This channel will point to the LIVE environment and using this will retain and add progress to your LIVE account as if you were playing normally. The best way to play on HOTFIX is to rename your LIVE folder to HOTFIX and verify using the HOTFIX channel on the launcher. Reverse this process to go back to LIVE once it is released or you would like to stop using this channel.

title: Re: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (4.6 Updates)
summary: No, your headset and OpenXR needs to be ready when starting the engine. Reason for that is that Vulkan needs to enable some extensions coming from OpenXR. Technically it is feasible, but this is extremely difficult to pull off since it requires to shutdown the graphics api completely and reinitialize it. Thats why you have to restart the engine as well when changing from Vulkan to DX11 or vice verca.

title: RSI Launcher 2.12.1 Release Notes
summary: Hello everyone,   Today, we are releasing the RSI Launcher 2.12.1.   RSI Launcher can be found here:  https://install.robertsspaceindustries.com/rel/2/RSI%20Launcher-Setup-2.12.1.exe    In this version, we added a VR option in the settings to enable/disable the game to detect your VR setup.   If you want to play Star Citizen in VR, please go to your game settings and enable VR. Once enabled you will see a “VR mode enabled” message mentioned under the channel selector. You can also disable it quickly in the gear of the Channel selector. On you first attempt if you encounter an issue with the VR feature, please clear your launcher cache. In Application Setting, click Clear Launcher Cache or using the key bindings: 'ctrl+alt+shift+r'.    :bug: Known issues:  Some users encounter a flickering Launcher background, which can be partially mitigated by turning off accessibility settings. title: Alpha 4.6 - Introducing New Industrial Missions
summary: Today, we're introducing a new set of Industrial missions designed to give industrial-focused players more freedom, more variety, and more reasons to explore. You may have already tested an early version of these when first introduced in the PTU 4.6 11022825, and even shared your feedback. If you did, thank you! It helps the teams a lot to further refine the content we release to the Live environment.  These  missions are designed to grow with you. Early contracts provide clear  guidance to help you learn the fundamentals, while advanced missions increasingly reward knowledge, planning, and creative problem-solving. Whether you prefer mining, salvaging, scavenging, refining, pirating, or finding alternative solutions, these contracts are designed to let you approach each job your way. How Do These Missions Work These Industrial missions are procedurally generated and available across Stanton, Pyro, and Nyx.  Each contract comes from a Mission Provider with a specific need; They care about results, not methodology. The mission does not spawn resources or mark exact locations. Instead, you are asked to use the sandbox to determine how and where to acquire what is needed.  If you already know where to source a material efficiently, you can act on that knowledge. If not, investigation, exploration, and discovery become part of the experience. Contract descriptions may include subtle hints to help narrow down potential sources.    Supported Industrial Paths These missions support a wide range of industrial gameplay loops and encourage players to mix and match approaches: Mining - Gathering minerals to refine (Raw Ore will be introduced at a later date) Salvaging - Collecting Recycled Materials Composite (RMC), components, and salvage Refining - Delivering refined ores and construction materials Scavenging - Recovering vehicle components and weapons Pirating - Scanning other ships and stealing their valuable cargo Hauling - Purchasing requested commodities directly from markets In some cases, alternative approaches are also viable. Purchasing materials through the economy or acquiring them through more aggressive means can be valid solutions, depending on the contract.   Let's get started! MINING Open your mobiGlas and go to the Contracts menu. You'll automatically receive your first tutorial mission for Hand Mining. Follow the mission instructions and travel to the specified location. Once you arrive, you will be asked to mine a few minerals. Don’t forget to bring a Multi-Tool with a Mining Attachment, which can be purchased at locations such as Kel-To, Refinery Decks, or similar shops.  Use your ship’s scanner to locate valuable resources in the area and gather the required materials. Follow the mission steps to deliver the collected cargo to the designated location and complete the contract.  You will then unlock additional missions, which will continue to expand as your reputation with the contracting faction increases. SALVAGING Salvaging missions are available under the Salvage category in your mobiGlas Contracts. They begin with Adagio Holdings, who are looking for sharp-eyed contractors capable of identifying salvageable materials, efficiently stripping them, and delivering Recycled Material Composite (RMC) and salvaged components.  Doing so will unlock additional missions for you to run, rewarding you as you progress through the faction's reputation. Feedback These Industrial missions represent an important step in expanding long-term gameplay for Star Citizen, and your experience matters. Now that they're live, we're eager to hear what works, what doesn't, and how these contracts fit into your playstyle.  You can share your feedback on Spectrum.

Inspired by Yuri and Corazon's timeless story of love and devotion, Coramor has become a celebration of connection, whether that's exchanging gifts with loved ones, traveling to new destinations, or reaching out across the void to those who matter most.   From now through February 23, celebrate what makes you smile: the people in your life, your favorite ship, and the moments that become your story. title: Love, Actually: Stories of the 'Verse 2956 Contest
summary: Coramor has always reminded us that behind every signal sent into the black is a story worth hearing.   This year, we want yours: not just the big moments, but also the ones that stayed quietly with you. The ones that made you smile. The ones that made you swallow hard. The ones that made you laugh at how ridiculous something was.  We want to hear the story that found you when you weren't looking, the moment you realised: Oh. I actually love this.  Your story. In your own words. No AI, no generators, no shortcuts, just you. Let it be the kind that makes someone say, 'I've felt that too.'  We're not looking for perfect prose. We want the truth of it: honest, raw, funny, whatever it is. Stories people can't fake because they're shaped by real moments, real connections, real 'verse magic.  If it's real, we'll feel it.   Welcome to the 'Love, Actually: Stories of the 'Verse 2956 Contest'! What We're Looking For The stories you carry with you: The ship that became home The wingmate who showed up at just the right time and never left The org that became an unexpected family The view that stopped you cold The cargo run where everything went wrong, but somehow became unforgettable That one moment, quiet, chaotic, or unexplainably perfect, that just... stuck with you Not just romance: stories of appreciation, awe, belonging, connection, triumph, or heartbreak.   If it tugged your heart or made you realise you care, we want to hear it.    Before You Begin   :exclamation: Before you start on your submissions, please read the contest rules carefully and remember to post your entries on the Community Hub. Replies to this thread will NOT count as entries.  NOTE: Submissions should be a 'Text' post and titled 'Love, Actually: Stories of the 'Verse 2956 Contest'. :exclamation:     Keep In Mind Read the contest rules! :book: Please post your submissions to the Community Hub Select the 'Text' post category Title your post: 'Love, Actually: Stories of the 'Verse 2956 Contest' Stories must be original and human-written. AI-generated content will not be considered (though grammar/spelling corrections are fine) Stories must be in English and related to your experiences in the 'verse Maximum 500 words One submission per person  Group entries are not allowed Submit your posts carefully, as posts edited after the submission deadline will not be considered. If you have made an error in the post, you can edit it provided this is done within the official duration of the contest Any submission not following the above instructions will NOT be considered   Winning Conditions The CIG jury will judge your submissions on: Quality Creativity Execution Emotional impact   Dates The submission period will end on Monday, February 23, 2026 at 20:00 UTC.    Prizes :first_place_medal: 1st Place: Argo MOTH in-game ship with LTI (Lifetime Insurance) + Lovestruck paint :second_place_medal: 2nd Place: MISC Fortune in-game ship with LTI (Lifetime Insurance) + Lovestruck paint :third_place_medal: 3rd Place: RSI Salvation in-game ship with LTI (Lifetime Insurance) + Lovestruck paint    :heartpulse: :black_heart: :heartpulse:   The 'verse is full of stories. This Coramor, send us yours.  We'll be listening. Happy Coramor, Citizens.   ---  UPDATE: We asked for your stories. You absolutely delivered.   Going through every single submission was genuinely one of the highlights of this contest for the team. Every entry that made the finalist shortlist did so because it had something real in it: funny, gut-punching, chaotic, tender. Sometimes all four at once.    The deliberation was... let's say emotional. Hankies were deployed. Feelings were had. That's how good your stories were.   Thank you all for sharing them with us. We heard each and every one of you.   Now, your Coramor 2956 winners:   :first_place_medal: First: @Daedalusflies - Community Hub Submission :second_place_medal: Second: @JessicaShtebs - Community Hub Submission :third_place_medal: Third: @Steadpaw - Community Hub Submission   Rewards will be coming to the winners in the next few days. Fly safe out there. :heart:

title: [4.6.0 LIVE Feedback] Argo MOTH

The Argo MOTH has been introduced to LIVE, which is a medium salvaging ship that has tools to earn its keep, the storage for a long job, and the ambition to take your team to an elevated tier of performance. And we'd like to hear what you think! More specifically we'd love to hear your thoughts on its salvaging ability, tuning, handling, interior, and general design of the ship.  In addition to this feedback thread we have opened a survey form for you to fill out! This includes some specific questions and can be found at: Argo MOTH Survey Form. This survey will be open until Feb. 25, however this thread will remain open for you to discuss your thoughts.  We look forward to reading your feedback!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: Roadmap Roundup - February 11, 2026
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.  With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!  -CIG Community Team Release View 4.6.0 New Resource Gathering Missions Implementing an expanded list of missions to our Resource Gathering archetype. Find, gather and deliver raw or refined mineable ores or salvageable ship pieces for a variety of corporations. Scheduled to come in a 4.6.x patch. :scroll: This card has been set to Released. Argo MOTH Implementing Argo’s new medium salvager: The MOTH has the tools to earn its keep, the storage for a long job, and the weaponry to work unencumbered. :scroll: This card has been set to Released.  Medical Light Armor "Chiron" Implementing the new Medical Light Armor "Chiron", a reward for the new 4.6 event Clearing the Air. :scroll: This card has been set to Released.   4.7.0 Claw Salamanders Faction Outfits Implementing multiple outfit variants for the Claw Salamanders gang in Nyx: A complete Light Armor, a cape, and a mask. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Heavy Combat Armor Implementing a heavy combat armor in the persistent universe. :scroll: This card has received a new visual.  Light Combat Armor Implementing a rework of a light combat armor in the persistent universe. :scroll: This card has received a new visual.     Progress Tracker We've updated a few deliverables in the Progress Tracker, which you can review below. Just a reminder: when progress on a deliverable is marked as complete, it doesn’t necessarily mean it’s ready for release. It may still require downstream support, transition to another team for further  work, or other additional steps before completion.   Crafting T0 Implementing the ability for players to craft various items using resources from throughout the persistent universe. :scroll: Extended to March 27th, 2026  Inventory Rework Implementing an improved experience with Inventory Management. :scroll: Extended to March 27th, 2026  Vehicle Command Module Introducing the concept of vehicles taking over control from other host ships. Primarily used for spaceships like the Drake Caterpillar or the Drake Ironclad. :scroll: Extended to May 29th, 2026  FPS Radar & Scanning Introducing improved signature system, supporting much greater distances, and dampening of signatures by environmental interference and larger signatures. title: Re: Devs Please! - Infinite Loading for last 14 Months!
summary: Things like this can be a bug with the game, or tech support issues. Hard to know which it is without troubleshooting it.   Easiest way to tell the difference between the two is to identify a computer that is able to log into the game ( physically going over a friends place, etc. ), and then log in with the account that's having issues. Knowing if it does or does not work on a computer where another account is able to log into the game is a useful piece of information to have when debugging things like this. Unfortunately, doing this is also not a great security practice since if that second computer is compromised with malware, it may cause account information to be compromised.  So barring that, usually step one for something like this is going to the tech support forum. A lot of the regulars there can help out with various problems. In order for this to be something that I forward to our developers to look at as a bug, we have to be sure that it's not a tech support problem. I can't convince a producer to take a developer off what they're working on without that.   With regards to the customer service tickets, I used to be able to help with those back in the day when our teams were smaller but since the company has expanded, I don't have access to those anymore. They may have a better idea on how to help you with this than I do.   Side note: the fact that you're getting the 'admin kicked' error sounds like your account might be stuck creating the character. The character repair tool might help with that if that's the case.   I'm going to take a look at the logs on our end just in case there is something I can find.
