title: Re: Positive Exchange of Flight Controls
summary: Heya, the topic of co-pilot seats and what those seats can actually do comes up quite often.  Right now we're somewhat limited what we can do as we have a static setup of which seat gets control over what functionalities at what point and there is no such thing as shared ownership. E.g. at any point there is only one seat that gets control over the flight controller (which is the entity that grants access to the thrusters, flight system, etc.) and we do not have a system in place that can purposefully swap control or parts of it over.  In the F7CM e.g. you can fly the ship perfectly normally from the back seat until the front seat is taken at which the control is handed over to the front seat (as the pilot seat has a higher priority over flight items). So right now, the architecture in that regard is a bit too rigid for purposeful (i.e. player controlled) dynamic swapping. The same accounts for systems like counter measures. Atm there is only player having authority over it but CMs would actually be a good case to allow control about for several players at the same time.  I absolutely agree with the use cases you listed (I'm personally a big fan of instructor two seaters, it's e.g. my favourite way to introduce players to VTOL VR which handles that case in a really nice way) and going even beyond that, I can imagine cases where you purposefully lock out functionalities out of seats via hacking or because your ship got boarded or so (a TNG "battle bridge" comes to mind). There is a lot of potential gameplay to be uncovered there.  So obviously we want to improve things long term but in the current list of things to achieve it sit's a bit lower in the priority list as it's a chunky piece of work. Hope that makes sense.

title: Re: MOTH's release state is a disaster
summary: Hey everyone,  Quick update on the current issues affecting the Argo MOTH.  Thanks for the reports here on Spectrum and the Issue Council contributions. They have been very helpful in tracking the issues down.   Some Top Issues, Currently Under Investigation It doesn't mean that other issues are not being investigated. These are currently the top reported issues, we will continue to monitor the situation. Salvaging at incorrect rates - The teams are currently reviewing the system. Not Auto Ejecting Cargo once filler station reaches SCU required for boxes External cargo weight issue Smaller ships unable to fracture larger ships Floating assets beside the pilot and the co-pilot seat Disintegration SFX persists Bed logging Lights behavior   Fixed internally, Expected In 4.7 The following issues are already resolved internally, and should be fixed in 4.7. Total filler station is smaller than intended Lost control when co-pilot is seated Pilot seat scan does not work when another player is on the salvage turret seat The railings of cargo bay have no collision  We appreciate the patience while we work through these. A good number of the most disruptive issues are already resolved for 4.7, and we will continue to monitor new reports as they come in.  Please keep the feedback and detailed repro steps coming on the Issue Council. It helps the teams to accelerate our process.  Cheers

With good fortune on your side this Red Festival, we’re challenging you to pull off your most clever maneuvers on foot or aboard your most agile ride for a chance to be rewarded in our community contest. Think tight spaces. Risky routes. Hard-to-reach locations all in the goal of prosperity. The kind of shots that feel earned, not staged, and make other citizens stop and ask: “How did you even get there? How did you do that?”  If luck favors the clever, now’s the time to prove it. If it took planning, precision, or a little audacity to pull off, you’re on the right track. title: Lunar New Year 2026 - Red Festival 2956
summary: Hi everyone,  Launch into the Lunar New Year with a bold new adventure from February 17 through March 3.  The Red Festival is a celebration of renewal and remembrance rooted in old Earth traditions that marked the end of a lunisolar year. Celebrants honor the festival in different ways across the UEE, often by wearing red to symbolize good fortune, sharing stories with friends and relatives, enjoying long foods like calossk tentacles or red-dyed noodles, and exchanging gilded red envelopes representing prosperity in the year ahead.  To ring in a prosperous Year of the Rat in 2956, we’re inviting you to celebrate the Red Festival with us. title: Re: Issues with LODs, rendering and textures in 4.6
summary: Thanks for the tag. I’ve not seen this issue, so we’ll do some digging and report back. But it’s likely one of two things: 1. The new graphics settings are very different to before, and it may be that on 8GB GPUs you’re using a lower texture quality than the system auto assigned you previously. The streaming system is quite complex, but when theres too much content to fit then some textures need to be lower resolution, and depending on the art setup this can sometimes be too aggressive on some meshes.  2. We’ve been overhauling the streaming system to make it much faster, and it’s possible this is just a bug. It could also be a combo of 1 & 2, ie a bug that is most evident when the system is pushed hard.   Cheers,  Ali Brown

title: [ETF NDA] Star Citizen Alpha 4.7 11368704 PTU Patch Notes
summary: Star Citizen Alpha Patch 4.7 Alpha Patch 4.7 has been released to Evocati, and is now available to test!   Patch should now show: VERSION 4.7.0-PTU.11368704. Audience: Evocati Only (Standard ETF NDA - Talk but no show) Timeframe: This will be a timed playtest. We are intending to leave this build up at least 6 hours (possibly overnight) Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only Long Term Persistence: Enabled (Please let us know of any early LTP issues between ptu builds) Note: This patch does not contain all of the intended features, which will be added iteratively to the notes as they become available. Additionally, some features may be implemented in a partial state and as such are not ready for testing and subject to removal.  When those features reach a playable state they will be detailed on the notes and added to the "Testing Focus".  Please issue council all issues related to those in testing focus and in general gameplay.   Testing/Feedback Focus Tonight’s build will be a timed playtest focusing as much as possible on the Rock Cracker Dungeon locations and their missions and sandbox activities. As tradition, keeping information about how to play somewhat limited for this first playtest to gauge in came communications on the location flows but will have more info in later PTU patches. Reminder: No PVP without agreeing during Evocati only builds! Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases Rock Cracker Operation and QV Breaker Stations  Known Issues Due to the mission locations not resetting upon restreaming the location, we are keeping this to a timed playtest PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations - Mission locations do not reset upon restreaming the location PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Design / Interactables - Screen is missing an interaction prompt for the Catalyst rack in Warehouse Control Room PU - Nyx - RCD - Location / Design - Lasing Catalysts can't be detached from the Monorail PU - Nyx - RCD - Location / Design - Some Mineable in the Asteroid can spawn in the walls  PU - Nyx - RCD - Props / Tech Design - powercell loses collision and can no longer be attached to item ports after being detached from the monorail PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Design / Interactables - Printer hopper closes and screen loses power after printing one lens PU - Nyx - RCD - Design / Locations - ReplaceMe textures on terminals in Operations near the array code PU - Nyx - RCD - Medical Screens / Locations / Medical - Medical imprint cannot be set at the Exclusive Medical Bay locations PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Art / Proxy - Breakable Ice entity visibly stays intact after shooting icicles    Features & Gameplay Gameplay Rock Cracker Operation - Breaker Stations The Rock Cracker Dungeon is a sandbox Location Event based in Nyx that will utilize new Asteroid Mining Stations to task players with rebooting one of these derelict stations so they can mine a large mineral resource at the center of the asteroid. This will primarily be a PVE focused sandbox activities with players fighting NPCs and creatures that have infested the dungeon during the course of restoring the station’s mining capabilities. For feedback focus, this dungeon experience is designed with 4-6 players in mind.  These locations can have sandbox activities that include interior missions such as recover item, missing person, and eliminate specific and exterior missions to recover cargo, kill ship bounty, support attack ship, and ship wave attacks.  There are currently 60 Exclusive Rockcracker locations, 30 Contested Rockcracker locations, and 20 General Mission Rockcracker locations. title: Re: Tomato-esque follow up for Sean Tracy
summary: Hi @SeriousFun, great to hear from you and glad you watched! Yeah, I would have loved to have a few more hours to talk deeper on some of the tool chains and other aspects of my work since we covered a very small percentage. I don't usually get on the forums here, but as you were so kind to me in person, happy to share what I can.  @SpaceTomato I watched the section of the video linked by @SeriousFun and happy to give some info.  RASTAR: Rastar indeed was the stepping stone to what has become Starchitect. Rastar suffered a bit of a problem on the onset, which was an small identity crisis!  It wasn't created by a tools team to start, although it started as a development tool. It quickly shifted to potentially being player facing, for things in the future.  Development-facing tools have totally different intentions than a player-facing tool would, imo. Although this is just my opinion, that was part of why it slowed down. Some lessons learned from it helped though, and much of the tech has made its way into Starchitect. So without diving too deep into it, Rastar has been used to get us as far as we are and is used to place some locations, but most if not all of the development-facing side has moved to Starchitect, which incidentally has been made explicitly with the updated Genesis model in mind and is more fit for purpose.  Houdini/MightyBridge: Still works! Great work from the MTL Tools group, honestly. It's quite sophisticated and still used in some regards to import Mighty Bridge Tools and live-connect the Editor to Houdini. Some tools/cases include:  Cover Tools: A tool to place cover objects around a selection of mesh in the Editor. Ledge Tools: A tool to automatically place ledges at the correct spots on each object you have selected. Cable Generator: Uses Houdini Vellum simulation to generate cables, using splines to create the base and objects in scene or planet surface as collision. Tarp Generator: Uses simulation to generate tarps, using splines to create the base cloth and objects in scene or planet surface as collision. Pile Generator: Allows you to create simulated piles of objects that are affected by gravity and ground collisions from any selection in the Editor. It can also scatter and duplicate them along a spline or in a specific direction. SplineInstancerTool: A tool to place different objects on a spline with different modifiers.  I love telling you guys about how we are putting this stuff together and its changing more than you'd think it does based on technology, expectations and sometimes crazy ideas so totally understand the questions and hope that sheds a bit of light on the areas you wanted more information on.   -Sean "Criminal" Tracy

Ledge Tools: A tool to automatically place ledges at the correct spots on each object you have selected. Cable Generator: Uses Houdini Vellum simulation to generate cables, using splines to create the base and objects in scene or planet surface as collision. Tarp Generator: Uses simulation to generate tarps, using splines to create the base cloth and objects in scene or planet surface as collision. Pile Generator: Allows you to create simulated piles of objects that are affected by gravity and ground collisions from any selection in the Editor. It can also scatter and duplicate them along a spline or in a specific direction. SplineInstancerTool: A tool to place different objects on a spline with different modifiers. I love telling you guys about how we are putting this stuff together and its changing more than you'd think it does based on technology, expectations and sometimes crazy ideas so totally understand the questions and hope that sheds a bit of light on the areas you wanted more information on. -Sean "Criminal" Tracy

title: [Evo NDA] Star Citizen Alpha 4.7 11399345 PTU Patch Notes
summary: Star Citizen Alpha Patch 4.7 Alpha Patch 4.7 has been released to Evocati, and is now available to test!   Patch should now show: VERSION 4.7.0-PTU.11399345. Audience: Evocati Only (Potential for Wave 1  this weekend if build validates) Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only Long Term Persistence: Enabled (Please let us know of any early LTP issues between ptu builds) Note: This patch does not contain all of the intended features, which will be added iteratively to the notes as they become available. Additionally, some features may be implemented in a partial state and as such are not ready for testing and subject to removal.  When those features reach a playable state they will be detailed on the notes and added to the "Testing Focus".  Please issue council all issues related to those in testing focus and in general gameplay.  Testing/Feedback Focus Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases Operation Breaker Station and Locations Inventory Rework Inclusions Crafting / Material Distibution Inclusions Engineering / Vehicle Armor Updates Radar-Based Aim Assist  Known Issues Note: For this build, music around the PU is disabled Multi-System - PU - ASOP Terminal / Locations - Moving the mouse cursor over a different vehicle in the ASOP when attempting to deliver a specific vehicle will deliver the different vehicle instead Multi-System - PU - ASOP Terminal / UI - There is a chance that a blank information of the Vehicle may appear on Hangar Delivery Request using the ASOP Terminal PU - Multi-System - Location / Art / Lighting - Lighting is in the wrong state in multiple PU locations PU - Nyx/Levski - Transit - Going prone whilst in a moving Limbo Elevator Carriage, will cause the player to fall out of the carriage PU - Starmap / MobiGlas / UI - Starmap is zoomed into the ship when in a cockpit instead of showing the system or region of space in PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Design / Interactables - Screen is missing an interaction prompt for the Catalyst rack in Warehouse Control Room PU - Nyx - RCD - Location / Design - Lasing Catalysts can't be detached from the Monorail PU - Nyx - RCD - Props / Tech Design - powercell loses collision and can no longer be attached to item ports after being detached from the monorail PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Design / Interactables - Printer hopper closes and screen loses power after printing one lens PU - Nyx - RCD - Medical Screens / Locations / Medical - Medical imprint cannot be set at the Exclusive Medical Bay locations PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Art / Proxy - Breakable Ice entity visibly stays intact after shooting icicles   Features & Gameplay Gameplay Operation Breaker Station Polish Moved missions to ship mining contract category. Further location Art, LOD, lighting, and audio polish.  Inventory Redesign The inventory system has been fully redesigned to make managing and equipping items significantly faster and more intuitive.  - Two-Panel Layout The inventory now uses a two-panel layout. By default, your personal inventory opens on the left panel and any nearby external inventory opens on the right. The content of each panel is interchangeable. The same inventory cannot be open in both panels simultaneously. If you open your personal inventory on both panels, the left panel defaults to your backpack and the right to your core inventory.  - Nearby Inventories Other inventories within close proximity, including cargo containers, backpacks on the ground, and bodies, are now automatically detected when you open the inventory. These appear as selectable tabs across the top of the UI, letting you browse and transfer items between them without having to separately interact with each container. Hovering over a tab will highlight the corresponding container in the world. If the container is off-screen, a small arrow indicates its direction. Inventories accessible through dedicated terminals, such as the item bank and freight elevator, are handled separately and are not part of the nearby inventory tab system. Two players cannot have the same inventory open at the same time. If another player is already using an inventory, its tab will appear greyed out and unavailable until they leave.  - Equipment Panel and Paper Doll An equipment panel sits on the left side of the UI and shows your currently held item and holstered weapons and tools. Weapon attachment slots are visible for your currently held item. Clicking a slot in the equipment panel filters the inventory panels to only show items that are valid for that slot.  The paper doll character view appears at the center of the screen. You can zoom in and out with the mouse wheel.  - Moving and Equipping Items Items can be dragged and dropped between inventory panels, onto equipment slots on the paper doll, or towards your feet to drop them on the ground. Right-clicking an item opens a context menu with options to Equip, Open Inventory, Hold, Rename, and Drop.  Dragging an item from an external inventory or from the paper doll into your personal inventory panel will automatically place it in your backpack first, then your core inventory, then legs, in that priority order.  - Search, Sort, and Filter A search bar lets you find items by name within the currently displayed inventory. You can also sort items by SCU size or item name, and apply category filters to show or hide particular types of items.  - Stack All A Stack All button lets you automatically combine all stackable items within an inventory in a single action. Items must be truly identical to stack, meaning same stats and same wear state.    Crafting Crafting is now available in Star Citizen, allowing players to use gathered materials to produce items via a new deployable machine called the Item Fabricator.  - The Item Fabricator The Item Fabricator is a placeable crafting station that can be purchased from refinery shops and retrieved through the freight elevator. Once placed in a hangar or base, it serves as the central hub for crafting and dismantling activities. The machine's door must be closed before it can be moved with a tractor beam.  - Blueprints All crafting is done through blueprints, which define what materials are needed and what the output will be. Players begin with a set of default blueprints already on their account. Additional blueprints can be earned as mission rewards and will appear in the Fabricator once obtained. Since adding crafting to 4.7, blueprints are randomized between dozens of different missions ranging from Gilly to FPS to industrial missions with certain bigger missions giving exclusive blueprint chances on completion. Blueprints are bound to the player's account and are retained through death.  - Material Quality All mineables gathered through mining now have a quality value. This value can be viewed in the mining UI, inventory, and the crafting interface. Quality is preserved when materials are refined (for example, turning Iron Ore into Iron carries the quality rating through to the refined output). The quality of materials placed into a blueprint directly influences the resulting item's stats, so higher quality inputs yield better performing outputs.  - Crafting an Item To craft an item, open the Fabricator and select a blueprint. Each blueprint displays the required material slots alongside which stats each slot influences. Players can manually assign materials to slots or use the auto-fill option to automatically populate slots with either the best or worst available materials. Double-clicking a material will place it into the first valid slot automatically. Slots may have minimum quality requirements and will not accept materials below that threshold. Materials can be freely removed from slots before confirming the craft.  Before confirming, players can set a delivery location for the finished item, either to a local inventory if within range or to the machine's cargo grid. The selected delivery location is remembered when switching between blueprints. Crafted items display their specific crafted stats in the tooltip.  - Crafting Queue Upon starting a craft, players are taken to the queue view. The Fabricator maintains separate queues for crafting and dismantling. Queued items can be moved between in-progress and pending states, and delivery locations can be adjusted per item. The machine also keeps a history tab showing previous completed jobs.  - Dismantling Items that have a crafting recipe associated with them can be dismantled in the Fabricator to recover materials. Items that were originally crafted by a player will return materials at the same quality used to make them. Items found in the world rather than crafted, such as looted weapons, will return materials at a flat default quality value.  - Material Distribution Overhaul There has been a large update to the distribution of ship and FPS mineables with the goal of making it easier to find a particular resource, particularly for ship mineables. Pyro has an increased chance of higher quality materials.  Please note, this is not of course final. Mineable distribution will be changed with planet tech v5 later down the line.  For ship mineables, all rocks are now 1 resource + inert. Across the board, the amount of SCU of resources within rocks has been reduced. As a general rule for ship mineables, the more valuable the resource, the smaller the SCU size. There are some drastic reductions in the cases of high value materials. Janalite has been added to the surface of some planets and moons. Mineable locations have been updated on planet / moon starmap records.

title: Re: [Evo NDA] Star Citizen Alpha 4.7 11399345 PTU Patch Notes
summary: Ships and Vehicles Engineering Gameplay - Shield Balance  Increased overall shield health. Shield variances have been brought a little closer together. Energy weapons will now damage shields more.  - Armor Balance There is now a minimum damage threshold for projectiles penetrating vehicle armor. This means that ship roles will play a much higher part in damaging higher armored ships. Armor at full health will block certain projectiles from damaging the armor, ship, and components. Armor once brought down to a lower health state will allow smaller bullets to damage the ship and components.   - Life Support Increased Life Support cost to maintain atmosphere. Decreased the exchange rates from Life Support to the room. Decreased the exchange rates between rooms.  - Radar Assigned power affects the aim assist. Increased power demand for all Radars. Activation power is either the same or lower. CS is only picked up on ping. New Radar items created that should be available in game.   Radar-Based Aim Assist Aim Assist Range Now Tied to Installed Radar  Ship aim assist is now governed by the radar equipped in your vehicle rather than applying uniformly at a fixed distance. The effective engagement window is determined by the power tier and model of your installed radar, defining both the minimum and maximum distances at which aim assist activates. Upgrading to a higher-grade radar will extend the range at which aim assist engages targets, while smaller or lower-powered units will support assist only at closer combat distances.  Aim assist now also includes a retention buffer. Once aim assist has locked onto a target within range, it will remain active for a short additional distance beyond the listed maximum before disengaging, preventing it from flickering on and off during close-range maneuvering at the edge of its effective range.  - New Radar Variants Added A large number of new radar variants have been added across multiple manufacturers and ship sizes (S0 through S3), significantly expanding loadout customization options. Each variant has been individually tuned with distinct aim assist range profiles to reflect its grade and intended role. Recon-focused units tend to prioritize extended engagement windows, while combat-optimized models offer tighter, more aggressive assist profiles.  The following manufacturers have new radar variants available: ·  Basilisk has new S1 and S2 combat models including the Prophet and Cassandra variants ·  CHCO has an expanded S0 through S4 lineup including FullSpec, BroadSpec, and Observer variants across multiple grades ·  Garuda/Gorenberg has new S0 through S3 options including the Tige, Vigilance, Savoir, Fidele, Resolu, and Devoue models ·  Navegante has new S1 and S2 sensor arrays including the SNSR5, SNSR7, and extended variants ·  Wilon has new S0 through S3 options including the Abetti, Agrippa, Anysta, Capsulo, and Socoria models     Bug Fixes Potential Fix: Multi-System - PU - Inventory Rework / Inventory / UI - Proximity detection is not working for all inventories Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD – Locations / Interactions – The fuse and repair doors inside the QV Breaker Station do not open even after a fuse is inserted and the door panel interacted with, blocking mission progression Potential Fix: PU - UI - Inventory Rework / Crafting - Crafted Items do not display their Crafted Stats in their Inventory Interface Descriptions  Potential Fix: VR Implementation - Fixed broken gasclouds in VR Potential Fix: Fix HUD for Atlas Mechs in VR. They wont move with the camera and are further away and scaled up - Force EHACM_DirectOffset in mechs/ATLS, so the arm can be moved properly Potential Fix: MultiVehicle - PU - AI - Radar - AI do not care about radar pip distances and will fire at players Potential Fix: PU - The entity count in the Nyx Space territory is abnormally high Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - Nyx Mission Pack 2 - Missions / Courier / Mission Content - Item packages for the FTL Courier missions are not spawning at the Pick Up Locations in Levski Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD - VFX / Locations - Snow kickup from footsteps is not affected by gravity   Technical Fixed 2 Client Crashes Fixed 2 Server Crashes

title: Re: OpenXR for VR
summary: Its not on us to fix this. I think the OpenXR Toolkit is just outdated and doesn't work anymore with newer Openxr versions. I could be wrong.  You can put sys.OpenXR.Layer.DisableOpenXRToolkit=0 in your user.cfg and play around and check if you can get it too work. Many people crashed when they had it installed so i disabled it in code, but using that cvar reverts this behavior.
body_html: Its not on us to fix this. I think the OpenXR Toolkit is just outdated and doesn't work anymore with newer Openxr versions. I could be wrong. You can put sys.OpenXR.Layer.DisableOpenXRToolkit=0 in your user.cfg and play around and check if you can get it too work. Many people crashed when they had it installed so i disabled it in code, but using that cvar reverts this behavior.

title: [Wave 1 PTU] Star Citizen Alpha 4.7 11414557 PTU Patch Notes
summary: Star Citizen Alpha Patch 4.7 Alpha Patch 4.7 has been released to the PTU!   Patch should now show: VERSION 4.7.0-PTU.11414557. Audience: Wave 1 Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only Long Term Persistence: Enabled (Please let us know of any early LTP issues between ptu builds) Note: This patch does not contain all of the intended features, which will be added iteratively to the notes as they become available. Additionally, some features may be implemented in a partial state and as such are not ready for testing and subject to removal.  When those features reach a playable state they will be detailed on the notes and added to the "Testing Focus".  Please issue council all issues related to those in testing focus and in general gameplay.  Testing/Feedback Focus Tonight's build will also have Nyx mission pack 2 enabled which will have existing mission types that send players to QV Breaker Stations around Nyx (these locations will not have the rock breaker activity) Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases Operation Breaker Stations and QV Breaker Stations locations Inventory Rework Crafting Fabricator and Blueprints Engineering Updates Radar Assisted Targeting (Radars components in shops will be arriving in a future PTU patch)  Known Issues Multi-System - PU - ASOP Terminal / Locations - Moving the mouse cursor over a different vehicle in the ASOP when attempting to deliver a specific vehicle will deliver the different vehicle instead Multi-System - PU - ASOP Terminal / UI - There is a chance that a blank information of the Vehicle may appear on Hangar Delivery Request using the ASOP Terminal PU - Nyx - RCD - Location / Design - Laser Catalysts can't be detached from the Monorail PU - Nyx/Levski - Transit - Going prone whilst in a moving Limbo Elevator Carriage, will cause the player to fall out of the carriage PU - Starmap / MobiGlas / UI - Starmap is zoomed into the ship when in a cockpit instead of showing the system or region of space in PU - Nyx - RCD - Medical Screens / Locations / Medical - Medical imprint cannot be set at the Exclusive Medical Bay locations PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Art / Proxy - Breakable Ice entity visibly stays intact after shooting icicles PU - Inventory Rework - UI - Inventory does not update Capacity and Space changes in Personal Inventory Multi-Item - PU - Inventory Rework / Weapons / Art - Some icons become stretched out upon scrolling down the inventory Multi-System - PU - UI / mobiGlas / Starmap - Starmap search bar dropdowns will only show location icons stacked on top of each other PU - Stanton - UI - Party marker does not show party members' names and distance   Features & Gameplay Gameplay Operation Breaker Stations Polish Reduced overall amount of Breaker Stations mission stations in Nyx. Large increase to buy-in cost for exclusive location access with reduced buy-in cost for non-exclusive. Ice Juvenile and Ice Adult Valakkar added and polished to Breaker Station locations. Increased respawn time for laser room combat AI. Performance updates with new meshes and LOD adjustments. Ambient audio adjustments. Temporarily added 3 more laser catalysts to processing room for PTU.   Inventory Redesign Added Apply/Clear buttons to the Search. Added support for fixed grid size specification for inventory UI items that does not change the size based on the orientation. Adjusted inconsistent use of dimensions throughout inventory system.  Crafting Fabricator & Blueprints Missions have been set up with their own blueprint pools allowing blueprints uniquely designated to specific missions. Added Vaughn FPS, Headhunters FPS, NorthRock, and BitZeros Blackbox recovery missions with blueprint pools. Added guaranteed blueprint chance for missions that give them. Further weapon blueprint inclusions. FPS Weapon and Armor blueprint rebalance based on rarity. Reduced default dismantle quality return and removed some blueprints from default list. Crafting UI adjustments to the button sizes and alignment. Implemented Paging support for UI to replace current scrolling mechanic. Updated fabricator queue screen to support updated UI. Adjusted recoil balance for crafted weapons.    Shop Price adjustments and additions Aegis Redeemer shop price greatly reduced Item Fabricator price increased Added Anvil Hornet F7CM Mk2 Ball Turret Updated MXOX Neutron Cannon S1, S2, S3 added Esperia Stinger and Grey's Market Shiv added to ship shops New ship rentals added: RSI Apollo Medivac and Triage, Esperia Prowler Utility, Drake Golem, MISC Fortune, and Aegis Avenger Titan. Added 2 handed tractor and salvage tool to more shops Ships & Vehicles Added limited gimbals to the Aegis Vanguard's nose gun Core Tech Music inclusion updates into 4.7 Further entity count updates in Nyx to reduce unintended high amounts   Bug Fixes Potential Fix: Fixed an issue of s1 weapons not being able to damage a lot of ships Potential Fix: Multivehicle - PU - Vehicles / Salvage - Reclaimer and Moth can fracture itself, causing it to explode (STARC-198054) Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations - Asteroid opening cap does not reset after completing the flow and restreaming the location Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD - Locations / Elevator Terminals - Service Entrance Elevator panels do not function at Shared and Sandbox locations Potential Fix: PU - Inventory Rework / Camera / Controls - When scrolling within the inventory on either the left or right panel, the paper doll camera zooms in and out (STARC-196034) Potential Fix: Item fabricator does not show the materials required to craft some items (STARC-198329) Potential Fix: RSI Apollo ALL Variants - PU - Vehicles / Vehicle Tech Art - The nose takes no damage as it is all passed up to the body Potential Fix: Crafting materials "stick" to the side of the screen if dragged off-screen Potential Fix: RSI Constellation Some Variants - PU - Vehicles / Elevators - Actor must jump to get on Elevator (STARC-120847) Potential Fix: Multi-System - PU - Recover Item / Courier - Nyx Mission Pack 2 - Mission Content / UI - Item port shows "No Appropriate Item" despite player holding mission critical box Potential Fix: Shader Eye in Specular Overlay render in front of the glass material (STARC-192503) Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD - Design / Interactables / Mission Content - Refractor Arrays are not being detected as powered upon activating them (STARC-198716) Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - Levski - Locations / Actor / Actor Status - Asphyxiation in Service Sections of Hangars (STARC-184322) Potential Fix: MultiVehicle - PU - Vehicles - The interaction range is too short on the weapon racks / lockers making it difficult for the user to place a weapon  Potential Fix: RSI Hermes - PU - Vehicles - The RSI Hermes Co-Pilot Seat is Missing (STARC-198062) Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD - Power Core - Location / Design - PGR Capacitor are removed from the slot if player push the lever when not all slot are filled Potential Fix: PU - Inventory Rework / UI - Unable to clear the local inventory search text due to the entered word disappearing (STARC-196025) Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD - Design / Locations - Interaction prompt on the other side of fuse doors is present and functional from the wrong side (STARC-198468) Potential Fix: APX Fire Extinguisher - PU - Weapons / Actor / Physics - Using the Fire Extinguisher causes the player to throw the Fire Extinguisher (STARC-198488) Potential Fix: PU - Nyx - RCD - Collision / Locations - Players can fall through the floor near the elevator door connector at Power Core Potential Fix: Multi-System - PU - Inventory Rework / Hangars / Containers -  Hangar Storage Kiosk allows player to drop large SCU cargo boxes through drop option (STARC-196141)   Technical Fixed 4 Client Crashes Fixed 4 Server Crashes Fixed multiple out of memory DGS issues

title: [4.7 PTU Feedback] Operation Breaker Stations
summary: Greetings!  4.7 introduces Operation Breaker Stations, which are a location based in Nyx that will utilize new QV Breaker Stations to task players with rebooting one of these derelict stations so they can mine a large mineral resource at the center of the asteroid. This will primarily be a PVE focused activity with players fighting NPCs and creatures that have infested the place during the course of restoring the station’s mining capabilities. For feedback focus, this PVE focused experience is designed with 4-6 players in mind.  A feedback survey is available at: Operation Breaker Stations Survey Form. This survey will be open until March 24.  We look forward to reading your feedback!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: [4.7 PTU Feedback] Fabricator Crafting System
summary: Greetings!  Crafting Fabricators have been added into 4.7, which allows you to craft a select amount of armors, fps weapons, ship weapons, backpacks, and more. These are crafted with Blueprints by utilizing materials you add to the fabricator. This implementation includes the ability to craft and queue items, dismantle crafted items, and more!  A feedback survey is available at: Fabricator Crafting System Survey Form. This survey will be open until March 24.  We look forward to reading your feedback!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: [4.7 PTU Feedback] Inventory Design Update
summary: Greetings!  The Inventory System has been reworked to give you even more control and flexibility over your gear. Instantly organize your inventory with one-click Stack All functionality, find items faster with natural language real-time search, much improved visuals, layout, performance, and more!  A feedback survey is available at: Inventory Design Update Survey Form. This survey will be open until March 24.  We look forward to reading your feedback!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: [4.7 PTU Feedback] People's Service Stations
summary: Greetings!  We have introduced a People's Service Statiosn in the Nyx system in 4.7. Managed by members of the People's Alliance, these service stations offer a safe haven with basic restock, rearm, and refueling operations for pilots traveling through Nyx.  A feedback survey is available at: People's Service Stations Survey Form. This survey will be open until March 24.  We look forward to reading your feedback!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: Roadmap Roundup - March 11, 2026
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.  With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!  -CIG Community Team Release View 4.7  All current 4.7 cards, except Nyx Missions (Pack 2), coming at a later date, have been set to Committed: New Hairstyles, Light Combat Armor, Heavy Combat Armor, Claw Salamanders Faction Outfits, Crafting T0, Inventory Rework, People's Service Stations, QV Breaker Stations, New Wikelo Ships Offerings (4.7.0), FPS Weapons Art Refactor, MaxOx Neutron Cannon Size 3.  MaxOx Neutron Cannon Size 3 Implementing a new Size 3 neutron weapon in the Persistent Universe: the MaxOx NN-15 Cannon. :scroll: This card has been brought to 4.7 PU, from 4.6 Arena Commander. :scroll: This card has been set to Committed.  FPS Weapons Art Refactor Updating visual material and texture for the following weapons and equipment: Behring: BR-2, GP-33, P8-AR, P8-SC, S-38 / Gemini: A03, C54, LH86, R97, S71 / Klaus and Werner: Arclight, Arrowhead, Demeco, Gallant, Lumin / Lightning Bolt Co.: Yubarev, Atzkav / Kastak Arms: Karna / APX Fire Extinguisher :scroll: This card has been set to Committed.  QV Breaker Stations Located in the Keeger Belt, QV Breaker Stations provide key infrastructure and operations, accessible through contracts: "QV Breaker Station Mining Rights", either "Exclusive" or "Shared". :scroll: The description has been updated to highlight Operation-type content. :scroll: The image has been updated. :scroll: This card has been set to Committed.  New Wikelo Ships Offerings (4.7.0) Adding a new vehicle and new equipment to the ever-expanding Wikelo's Emporium: RSI Apollo Triage, with upgraded components and a unique base livery. This reward can be unlocked by completing Wikelo's contracts. :scroll: The image has been updated. :scroll: This card has been set to Committed.  People's Service Stations Implementing social stations in Nyx. Managed by members of the People's Alliance, these service stations offer a safe haven with basic restock, rearm, and refueling operations for pilots traveling through Nyx. :scroll: The image has been updated. :scroll: This card has been set to Committed.

title: Re: No cursor and freezes
summary: Hey there! We have seen this set of symptoms a number of times recently, and it appears to be caused by the latest update to Overwolf, which is a software many people have installed at one point or another for other games.  Uninstalling Overwolf should do the trick, or alternatively some players mentioned that using Direct3D 11 instead of Vulkan also works, if you would like to keep it installed.  Some players encountering this issue also experience crashes instead of freezes when attempting to open or close menus, or when pressing F.

title: Stella Fortuna 2956 - "Good Luck, Full Speed, Respawn" Video Contest
summary: Stella Fortuna 2956 has arrived, and luck loves a little chaos :four_leaf_clover:  This year, we’re looking for 30-second video stunts that celebrate speed, risk, sharp turns, super-hero landings, or even glorious miscalculation. We want to see your wildest racing lines, your boldest jumps, your sketchiest recoveries, and your most spectacular crashes.  Whether you're sending a ground vehicle off a cliff and somehow landing it, surviving an impossible jump, threading an Argo CSV through a C1 Spirit on microTech, or drifting something that was never meant to drift: If it feels slightly irresponsible but absolutely legendary, you are doing it right.  Stella Fortuna is about trusting your instincts and committing to the play. Clean run or catastrophic failure, if it's bold and real, it belongs here.  Fortune favors the brave. Sometimes it favors the lucky. Let’s find out which one you are. How To Participate We are calling on the community to celebrate Stella Fortuna by showcasing high-risk stunt gameplay in a short-form video.  Please read the contest rules carefully to avoid disqualification. :four_leaf_clover: Plan the Chaos: Choose your ship or ground vehicle and design a stunt or race line that pushes limits. Think speed, danger, verticality, tight terrain, environmental hazards, or ridiculous ideas that somehow might work. :movie_camera: Capture the Moment: Record a 30-second in-game video. Keep it tight and focused. The stunt should be the star. :outbox_tray: Submit: Create a Stella Fortuna 2956 post in the Community Hub, submitted as a Video.   Keep In Mind! Read the contest rules! Posts must be submitted to the Community Hub, as a video hosted on YouTube Videos must not include any third-party music, AI-edited content, effects, sounds, soundtrack, or other third-party content. Star Citizen music and sounds are accepted. Visual post-processing effects are allowed, as well as on-screen graphics from the editing software of your choice. Videos must not include any other video, submission, contest entry, or other external content. Videos must include the provided end slate, shown for at least 3 seconds: https://media.robertsspaceindustries.com/qxub1wbq2zm6r/source.zip Maximum video length: 30 seconds, including the required end slate. Minimum video resolution: 1920 x 1080, but 3840 x 2160 (4k UHD) is highly preferred. Videos may have a maximum of three contributors or collaborators. You may include more players in the video, but only up to three people per submission are eligible to win. Submissions should clearly state the RSI handles of all those being credited as contributors or collaborators at the time of submission. Multiple submissions by or involving a participant are NOT permitted.   Preferred Tech Specs: VIDEO Format: .MP4 Codec: H.264 Aspect Ratio: 16:9 Frame Rate: 30fps (minimum) Pixel Dimensions: 3840 x 2160 4k UHD (preferred) / 1920 x 1080 (minimum) AUDIO Stereo, 48kHz, 24bit (16bit minimum)   Winning Conditions The CIG jury will judge your submissions on the following: Visual quality Creativity and originality of the stunt Execution and difficulty Strong interpretation of the Stella Fortuna theme, including risk, luck, and bold commitment   Dates The submission period ends on Monday, March 30, 2026, 20:00 UTC. Rewards :first_place_medal: 1st Place: Aegis Sabre Peregrine in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Star Kitten Racing" Livery Aopoa Nox in-game vehicle with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Star Kitten Racing" Livery Origin 350r Racing Suit Origin 350r Racing Helmet Fortuna Racing Suit Fortuna Racing Helmet P4-AR “Fortuna” Rifle  :second_place_medal: 2nd Place: Origin M50 in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Murray Cup" Livery Origin 350r Racing Suit Origin 350r Racing Helmet P4-AR “Fortuna” Rifle  :third_place_medal: 3rd Place: Mirai Fury LX in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and "Mirai Racing" Livery Fortuna Racing Suit Fortuna Racing Helmet P4-AR “Fortuna” Rifle  Good luck, full speed, and if you explode… Respawn! Winners :first_place_medal: 1st Place: @bolli51 @SuterPS @The_Floeffel embodied Stella Fortuna's "Good Luck, Full Speed, Respawn" fully, hitting every single box of the contest and making it look easy, well done! // Entry :second_place_medal: 2nd Place: @Boltok @COP_rider Holy Molly, I'm reassured to have you in my team for Crux Cup 24H. // Entry :third_place_medal: 3rd Place: @DriftwoodBadger @Aetherghoul Blink and you'll miss it, full speed! // Entry

title: Stella Fortuna 2956
summary: Hi everyone,  Stella Fortuna returns to the ‘verse, inviting you to chase that impossible score, take the long odds, and stake your claim on something bigger. This is the day when calculated risks turn into legendary wins, when daring crews make their own luck, and when fortune favors those willing to reach for it.  Across the UEE, Stella Fortuna marks the spirit of ambition and opportunity. What began as a celebration of humanity’s drive to push outward has become a tribute to those who bet on themselves, launch the ventures others won’t, and refuse to sit on the sidelines. In a universe shaped by risk, there is no better time to test your mettle.  Now it’s time to step forward and throw your name into the spotlight: this is your moment to tempt fate.  ► Visit the official Stella Fortuna 2956 page to get involved, from March 12 to March 30! ▲ Enjoy everything Stella Fortuna has to offer: Stella Fortuna 2956 - With a spirited contest, lively liveries, and track-inspired racing gear, you'll find plenty of ways to get your pulse racing. Video Contest "Good Luck, Full Speed, Respawn" - Send a ground vehicle flying off a cliff, thread an Argo CSV through a C1 Spirit, drift something that was never meant to drift. Tempt fate and show us your most chaotic, skillful, or ridiculous stunts for a chance to win rewards. Galactapedia - Learn more about the lore of ⁠Stella Fortuna March Subscriber Flair - Push your limits on the track and let the medical ships and flair keep you in the race! Arena Commander - Take to the racetracks in Arena Commander's Classic Race online mode and prove your mettle. Every pilot who competes will claim the Giocoso Helmet in Ivory (Rewarded at the end of the event) - no luck required. ATMO Esports & ANZIA Racing events - Feeling the need for speed? Join ATMO Esports for System 7 or push your ship to the limit with ANZIA Racing in the Crux Cup - two community race events you won't want to miss.

title: Alpha 4.7 - Patch Watch | System... Check!
summary: Hello everyone,  Welcome to another Patch Watch! These posts shine a light on upcoming features, improvements, and fixes that may not appear on the Public Roadmap but are updates we believe you will find valuable. You can also read the recent PTU Patch Notes for Alpha 4.7.  This time, we are focusing on several gameplay and balance updates coming to Alpha 4.7. From engineering tweaks to radar behavior, armor & shield balance, salvage variety, and missile balance, these changes aim to improve combat readability, ship survivability, and overall gameplay consistency.  Let's dive in! Engineering Gameplay Updates Alpha 4.7 brings a new round of balancing to shields and armor, aimed at improving combat pacing and ship durability.  Shield Balance Update These changes should make shield combat feel more consistent while reinforcing the intended strengths of energy-based loadouts when targeting shielded opponents. Increased overall shield health across ships Reduced the gap between shield variants to make their performance differences less extreme  Energy weapons will now deal increased damage to shields   Armor Balance Update This creates a clearer combat progression where heavier weapons or sustained damage are required to break through strong armor before lighter weapons can become effective. We are introducing minimum damage requirements for armor When armor is at full health, certain smaller projectiles will no longer damage the armor, ship hull, or internal components Once armor has been weakened and reaches a lower health state, smaller caliber weapons will begin to penetrate and deal damage On top of these, armor will get a general balance pass to take these new changes into account. For example, a Perseus has heavy armor, so a small ship weapon won’t be able to penetrate it or deal damage. However, once the armor has been weakened, a small ship weapon could then be able to affect the ship. You’ll need bigger guns to crack that tough shell first.   Life Support Adjustments Life Support systems are receiving tuning to better reflect the effort required to maintain ship atmospheres.  Increased Life Support cost to maintain the atmosphere Reduced the exchange rate between Life Support systems and rooms Reduced exchange rates between connected rooms Life Support generators will now also take longer to refill rooms and perform heat exchange In practice, this means atmosphere management becomes slightly more deliberate, especially on larger ships where room-to-room air exchange plays a bigger role.    Radar and Detection Changes The type of installed radar and the amount of assigned power now have a direct effect on the range at which aim assists and ESP come into effect. This is reflected by the lack of PIPs outside the effective range and by appropriate UI elements during precision targeting.  Power and Aim Assist Assigned power now directly affects aim assist range; this applies to both weapon aim assist and ESP. For example, assigning 2 points to your S1 Radar would set aim assist at 910 meters, while assigning 5 points would increase it to 1,105 meters.  This range is reflected on your HUD by the distance at which target pips appear, and it changes based on both the radar installed on your ship and the amount of power assigned to it.  Radars now require more sustained power to operate Activation power requirements remain similar or slightly lower Weapon aim assist and ESP are available when a target is within your effective assist range. Increasing power to your radar extends that range, while reducing power shortens it. This adds another layer to power management decisions during combat.   Precision Targeting Precision targeting is also affected by radar power and assist range. Subtargets are now visible during precision targeting when you are within a meaningful assist range Stronger radar power helps maintain that range, making precision targeting more reliable during combat  Cross-Section Detection Cross-section signatures are no longer passively detected They are now only detected through active pinging with your scanner  This change opens the door for fully stealth-focused builds.  New Radar Items New radar components have been created and are planned to become available through in-game shops, missions, and potentially crafting The manufacturers Basilisk, CHCO, Garuda/Gorenberg, Navegante, and Wilon offer new ship radars Cave Scanning Reliability The cave scanning setup has been reworked to make cave locations more reliable when scanning planets from your ship.  This should make it easier to locate caves for exploration, missions, or resource hunting without relying on inconsistent scan results.   Salvage Contract Improvements The salvage contract pool has been expanded to include additional ships.  Many of these ships are now Gold Standard and feature physicalized components, which means salvagers will encounter a wider range of recoverable materials and parts.  What this means for you: Greater variety in salvage targets More meaningful component recovery opportunities More dynamic salvage runs instead of repeatedly encountering the same ships Missile Balance and Ship Access Points A balance pass has been made for missiles and ship access points such as doors, ramps, and lifts.  Missile Changes Missile explosions will no longer damage internal components inside a ship.  Previously, anything within the explosion radius could take damage, including modules and internal systems located inside the hull. Because of this, explosion radii had to remain very small to prevent ships from being destroyed by a single hit.  With internal damage removed, missiles can now be balanced more naturally around their explosion radius.  The new balance gives players a clearer choice in how they want their missiles to behave: Direct: higher damage with a smaller explosion radius Area: lower damage with a larger explosion radius Damage values are also being adjusted, but overall balance should remain familiar. Specific values will shift slightly along the existing curve.  These adjustments also apply to ground vehicles.   Doors, Ramps, and Lifts Because missile explosion radii are changing, we also reviewed the durability of ship access points.  Many doors, ramps, and lifts currently have very low health values and were never properly tuned. Without adjustments, the new missile explosions could blow open a ship with a single hit, which would look odd and break immersion.  To address this, we are increasing their health to better match overall ship durability.  This should result in more believable damage behavior while still allowing access points to be destroyed under sustained fire.

For example, a Perseus has heavy armor, so a small ship weapon won’t be able to penetrate it or deal damage. title: Re: Request: Axis recenter keybind/console command
summary: Heya, we are not planning to add any calibration tools or hotkeys to recenter input devices. We rely on Windows for telling us what devices are there and what they put out in terms of data ... as this has been the standard for decades.  That said I do understand your problem, I also went through two sets of TFRP rudders within a couple of years. Generally higher priced ones are usually more rugged and that is really across all manufacturers. So you could maybe check if there are any tools like Joystick Gremlin or so that might offer some reset functionality. But in general, if the hardware is defect, then it's defect ... so you have to either get it repaired or replaced. Or repair it yourself if the warranty has run out. There is a lot of machinery around that really just needs a bit of a clean-up at times. And pedals will accumulate quite a bit of dust over time.

So you could maybe check if there are any tools like Joystick Gremlin or so that might offer some reset functionality. But in general, if the hardware is defect, then it's defect ... so you have to either get it repaired or replaced. Or repair it yourself if the warranty has run out. There is a lot of machinery around that really just needs a bit of a clean-up at times. And pedals will accumulate quite a bit of dust over time.

title: [4.7 PTU Feedback] Armor Rework
summary: Greetings!  4.7 introduces a rework for how armor works. There is now a minimum damage threshold for projectiles penetrating  vehicle armor. This means that ship roles will play a much higher part in damaging higher armored ships. Armor at full health will block certain projectiles from damaging the armor, ship, and components. Armor once brought down to a lower health state will allow smaller bullets to  damage the armor ship and components. We'd love to hear your thoughts on these changes, and your responses to: Where do you expect to find armor information? What is the top visual feedback that you think is missing right now? Do the current armor values match the expectations of individual ships or are there any ship outliers? What layer of visual feedback would help you the most at identifying weak points as valid targets on bigger ships to be identified?  E.g. turrets are not protected by the ships full armour.  A feedback survey is available at: Armor Rework Survey Form. This survey will be open until March 30.  We look forward to reading your feedback!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: Re: Why did LAMP stop getting added to ships?
summary: Hi all,  I wanted to provide a bit of context around why LAMP hasn’t yet appeared across more ships. Due to the way vehicles are built in Star Citizen, canopies typically consist of two panes of glass: an interior-facing pane and an exterior-facing pane. As you may have noticed, LAMP operates on the interior pane only, which means the effect is visible to players inside the cockpit looking outward. When ships are authored, there are two slightly different workflows for how the canopy and interior glass are set up depending on the ship:  Animated canopies – If the canopy needs to animate, the interior glass pane must be attached to the canopy itself, which is part of the vehicle’s exterior asset. Static canopies – If the canopy does not animate, the interior glass pane can instead be placed within the interior “object container,” meaning it is functionally separate from the exterior asset.  When LAMP was initially planned, the intention was to roll it out to the ten most-used single-seat ships. With support from the game code and graphics teams, we were able to automate much of the setup for ships that fall into the first category. As a result, those ships were relatively straightforward to support. Ships in the second category are more complex. Because the interior glass is not linked to the exterior canopy, LAMP cannot currently be applied using the same approach. We have raised work with the relevant teams to support this case, but the timing will depend on their broader priorities and scheduling. The positive news is that a potential path forward has been identified. We already have other systems that link similar assets, such as the canopy rain and snow effects, which will hopefully provide a framework to extend LAMP more broadly.   We did also explore an interim approach that would involve separating the interior glass pane and reattaching it to the exterior asset. However, applying this change across the remaining ships would require a significant amount of art and design time as well as the potential for introducing further issues such as undesired wear on interior glass panes. For that reason, a code-based solution is likely to be the cleaner and more sustainable approach in the long term.  We're looking forward to getting the rest of our ship lineup up to date with LAMP functionality and will keep you in the loop as we progress

title: Re: New flight system
summary: @Arcantelle, what we're doing atm is regular testing of the latest NFM builds with players, but these are in a closed environments. All players who participate are under NDA. We're doing that to get more focused playtest feedback. For every test we invite between 100 and 200 players to take part and after the test weekend access is revoked again. That's been going for some time now.  You cannot apply to take part in the testing, the selection is done based on whatever player profile we need for the test (e.g. truckers, racers, PVE players, etc.) and then players are randomly picked after a bit of filtering. We roll the dice every single time to avoid bias and when they sign the NDA, they get access to the next build.  And so far that has been working really well for us. We can easily playtest, try out variations, validate concepts and can put a lot of trust in the feedback. The iteration is much faster than it would be with public testing. We will keep doing it until we're ready to go full public. But we're not there yet.  Hope that makes sense, Yogi

We will keep doing it until we're ready to go full public. But we're not there yet. Hope that makes sense, Yogi

title: Re: New flight system
summary: The selection is random every time but we do not mark up players who already took part, so dependent on the selected group there might be some overlap.
body_html: The selection is random every time but we do not mark up players who already took part, so dependent on the selected group there might be some overlap.

title: Re: New flight system
summary: Just for NFM so far, but we might consider the same approach for other features.
body_html: Just for NFM so far, but we might consider the same approach for other features.

title: Re: New flight system
summary: In general, you do not need a lot of testers to uncover problems. Trends (be positive or negative) can easily identified with often just a handful of players and we usually have over a hundred in every test. Also it is not true that anything is set in stone, we've been constantly adapting the FM, updated the tuning, etc. ... you might disagree with certain design or tuning choices but usually they are done because they overall are better for the game.
body_html: In general, you do not need a lot of testers to uncover problems. Trends (be positive or negative) can easily identified with often just a handful of players and we usually have over a hundred in every test. title: Re: New flight system
summary: I got nothing super exciting for you ... the design pretty much stands, most of the work is mostly about finding the right tuning spot. And that's a bit of a grindy part. We're currently trying out variations of afterburner modifiers and one of the next tests will validate a couple of bug fixes on the motion processor limiters ...

title: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (Alpha 4.7)
summary: Hey everyone,  Hope you’re all enjoying the ’verse. We’ve got another round of VR improvements coming with Alpha 4.7, some of which you may have already noticed. Let’s dive in!   ATLS Mech UI The ATLS mech Geo UI is now functioning properly in VR. Stomp away.   Stereo Cursor Rewrite The stereo cursor has been completely rewritten. Instead of relying on screen-based offsets, it now accumulates mouse movement directly.  The result: no more boundary. Previously, the cursor was limited to a fixed screen region, creating an invisible wall. That limitation is now gone.  One thing to note: since the cursor is no longer tethered in the same way, it can move outside your field of view when decoupled from head movement. If it seems to disappear, simply toggle it again to recenter.   Separate UI Render Resolution This is a big one. The engine can now render UI at a separate resolution from the 3D scene. In practice, this means UI elements like the inventory and other full-screen interfaces now display correctly in VR.  This is controlled through two new cvars: r_StereoUIWidth r_StereoUIHeight The default is set to 2560x1440, which works well for headsets like the Quest 3. If you’re using a higher-resolution headset, you can increase these values for sharper UI. These settings can be adjusted at runtime, so feel free to experiment, including with widescreen resolutions. We may add this to the settings menu in the future. Changing the resolution will impact performance only very slightly. With that being said the Show Console (In VR) option is no longer needed and has been removed from the menu and is now on by default.   PlayerInteractionShortcut (PIS) Wheel No longer moves with the view and is always centered onto the UI screen. In the future this will be rendered in 3D space where the interactable is when we refactored the system.    Native Pimax OpenXR No Longer Blocked by EAC As many of you have discovered, the native Pimax OpenXR runtime is no longer blocked by EAC and can now be used freely. The main benefit here is improved performance. SteamVR can introduce noticeable overhead, so bypassing it should provide a meaningful boost.  Additionally, the native runtime may expose OpenXR features that SteamVR doesn’t support, opening the door to more possibilities for Pimax headsets moving forward.   What's Still in Progress Close-range markers are still a work in progress. This requires deeper changes from the UI Tech side, so it’s not something we can quickly patch. Thanks for your patience while we get this right.  At the moment, the Meta (Quest) Link runtime can cause reprojection artifacts with low framerates. We’re still investigating whether the XR_FB_space_warp extension can resolve this issue in the future. To prevent this in the meantime, you can disable the Asynchronous Spacewarp in the Oculus Debug Tool (usually found in C:\Program Files\Meta\Support\oculus-diagnostics\ or C:\Program Files (x86)\Oculus\Support\oculus-diagnostics\). This needs to be done each time you start Meta Quest Link.  As an alternative, we also recommend using Virtual Desktop if you have a capable WIFI router with a strong connection. On top of that you may also reduce the FOV Tangents slightly in the settings to improve GPU performance (i.e. tangents set to 90%).   That’s all for 4.7 for now. We’ll keep pushing on polish and new features for VR, so stay tuned. See you in the 'verse.

title: [4.7 LIVE Feedback] Armor Rework
summary: Greetings!  4.7 introduces a rework for how armor works. There is now a minimum damage threshold for projectiles penetrating  vehicle armor. This means that ship roles will play a much higher part in damaging higher armored ships. Armor at full health will block certain projectiles from damaging the armor, ship, and components. Armor once brought down to a lower health state will allow smaller bullets to  damage the armor ship and components. We'd love to hear your thoughts on these changes, and your responses to: Where do you expect to find armor information? What is the top visual feedback that you think is missing right now? Do the current armor values match the expectations of individual ships or are there any ship outliers? What layer of visual feedback would help you the most at identifying weak points as valid targets on bigger ships to be identified?  E.g. turrets are not protected by the ships full armour.  A feedback survey is available at: Armor Rework Survey Form. This survey will be open until April 8.  We look forward to reading your feedback!  -Shark Player Experience Team

title: Roadmap Roundup - March 25, 2026
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.  With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!  -CIG Community Team :information_source: We’ve preemptively marked the Alpha 4.7 cards as Released ahead of our scheduled LIVE publish happening later today.   Release View Alpha 4.7 All of the following 4.7 cards have been set to Released as part of Alpha 4.7 going live later today: New Hairstyles, Light Combat Armor, Heavy Combat Armor, Claw Salamanders Faction Outfits, Crafting T0, Inventory Rework, People's Service Stations, QV Breaker Stations, New Wikelo Ships Offerings (4.7.0), FPS Weapons Art Refactor, MaxOx Neutron Cannon Size 3, Ice Adult Valakkar, Ice Juvenile Valakkar.  Nyx Missions (Pack 2) has been set to Committed, and is planned for a later release in 4.7.x.  RSI Aurora Mk II Implementing the RSI Aurora Mk II, building upon RSI’s legacy as the starting point of exploration, progression, and expedition. :scroll: This card has been set to Released.  Ice Adult Valakkar Adding the Ice Adult Valakkar that players can find within QV Breaker Stations. :scroll: This card has been set to Released.  Ice Juvenile Valakkar Adding the Ice Juvenile Valakkar that players can find within QV Breaker Stations. :scroll: This card has been set to Released. Alpha 4.8 Refueling Missions Implementing refueling missions centered on servicing NPC ships. Players will also be able to request refueling via a beacon, which will initially be fulfilled by NPCs. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Refueling Improvements Implementing refueling and docking improvements, simplifying the refueling process with simplified fuel deliver and updating docking to support mutual requests and automatic docking at close range, alongside more impactful itemization for fuel capacity and transfer speeds. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Flight Suits G-Force Resistance Implementing G-Force resistance modifiers to flight suits, enabling players to choose specialized equipment for improved maneuverability and endurance. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Ship Hangar Service T0 Implementing service gameplay updates that draw from resources stored in your ship’s cargo grid to fulfill refueling, repair, and restocking requests via dedicated service hangars. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Vehicle Command Module Implementing Vehicle Command Module docking/undocking and ship systems transfer. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  New Wikelo Ships Offerings (4.8.0) Adding a Kruger L-22 Alpha Wolf with a unique base livery and upgraded components as a reward for completing a new addition to the variety of available Wikelo's Emporium contracts. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  UltiFlex Crossbow Implementing the long-awaited crossbow, featuring a devastating, shattering bolt and harsh projectile drop, the Ultiflex Crossbow rewards skilled aim with immense power. Its near-silent firing mechanism lets you strike quietly and gain the upper hand on your foes. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  KSAR Plasma Grenade Implementing Kastak Arms area-denial grenade. Prime and throw to lock down an area and prevent enemies from pushing through. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Transport System Implementing the new Transport System, a full rewrite of transit across the universe, supporting trams, trains, and elevators with improved reliability and scalability for technologies like Server Meshing and Instancing. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Aegis Hammerhead - Gold Standard Updating the Aegis Hammerhead to Gold Standard, and implementing improvements and updated interior art. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.   Star Citizen 1.0 Maelstrom Implementing a new physically based destruction system. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.

title: Operation Breaker Stations - FAQ
summary: "Hey everyone,  Shubin Interstellar would like to remind you that the QV Breaker Stations in the Nyx system are "technically" operational.  Just temporarily... unpowered. And possibly structurally compromised. Fully vacated by original personnel. Maybe." Scattered across the Keeger Belt, QV Breaker Stations once formed the backbone of asteroid mining operations in the region. Key infrastructure. Serious machinery. The kind of facilities that were never meant to go quiet... until one day they did. A few of them still look exactly as they were left. That was over three hundred years ago. Long enough for things to get complicated. They're still out there; your contract board will take you to one. What's waiting inside is yours to discover.   We've put together answers to some of your common questions about Operation Breaker Stations below.    Operation Breaker Stations – FAQ ▲ What is Operation Breaker Stations?  Operation Breaker Stations is a new repeatable PvE-focused activity arriving with Alpha 4.7: Welcome to the Rock. You'll be exploring derelict asteroid mining facilities in the Keeger Belt, finding your way through caverns, restoring power to a dead station, and ultimately firing an absolutely massive laser at a rock. You know. Normal Tuesday stuff.   ▲ How do I find a QV Breaker Station?  Don't bother checking the Starmap, these locations won't appear there. The only way in is through a contract. Accept a QV Breaker Station Mining Rights contract in your mobiGlas. These contracts are available through Shubin Interstellar and can be purchased for aUEC, but you'll need to build some rep with them first. Shared Rights contracts unlock at Rep 1, Exclusive Rights at Rep 2. Do some mining, earn their trust, and the contracts will follow. No rep, no contract, no station.   ▲ Can I replay this?  Yes! Repurchase your Mining Rights from Shubin Interstellar for aUEC and go again as many times as you like.     ▲ What types of Mining Rights contracts are there?  Two flavors: Shared Rights – Other players may be working the same site. Whether that turns into cooperation or chaos is entirely up to you lot. Requires Rep 1 with Shubin Interstellar. Exclusive Rights – The station is yours alone. Quiet. Unpowered and seemingly derelict, and no witnesses other players. Requires Rep 2 with Shubin Interstellar.   Note: Shared Mining Rights contracts are available from Levski and each People's Service Station across Nyx. There's plenty to go around, though some stations will be busier than others. If you're after a quieter run at a QV Breaker Station, it might be worth travelling a little further afield to pick up your contract.   ▲ Is this a solo or group activity?  Operation Breaker Stations is designed for groups of 4-6 players, though smaller crews and solo runs are possible. PvP is not the focus with this activity, though we can't speak for the general lawlessness of the 'verse. That is why there are two options (Exclusive or Shared Rights) to suit your preferred playstyle.   ▲ What rewards can I expect? A mix of FPS-lootable items and ship-mineable resources of varying rarities, dependent on how deep you go into the cracked asteroid. Complete the mission contract, and you'll also walk away with a blueprint — guaranteed, until you've collected them all.   ▲What do I need? Helmet (Never leave home without it.) FPS mining tool (This is super handy to have, trust us on this.) Tractor beam tool (Seriously, don't forget this.) Combat loadout (You know, just in case.) Medpens or Med Guns (Nice to have even though it's perfectly safe in there. Allegedly.) A nimble mining ship (You came to crack rocks. Don't leave empty-handed.)   ▲ How do I get around in a QV Breaker Station?  Besides your trusty two feet? Two transit systems exist within the facility. The Ring Shuttle connects the main facility areas and is your primary way of getting around the station. The Autonomous Monorail Transport runs between the Laser Head room and the Warehouse.    ▲ Walk me through what actually happens inside.  Glad you asked. Here's a short field guide: EVA In — The station's dead on arrival. Land on one of the two landing pads under the Laser Head and EVA through the Maintenance Entrance airlock. There's more than one way to navigate the facility once you're inside. Explore the Location — Hunt down various components scattered throughout the facility. You might meet some unfriendly locals along the way. Physical challenges, puzzles, hazards, loot. The works. Restore Power — Install missing components to the power bank in the Central Core to restore auxiliary power to the facility. Try to stay alive while doing it. Power Trip — Head outside via the airlock, call the Ring Shuttle, and ride it to the Operations Center. Do what you need to do to restore functionality to the facility. The Lights Are On. Now What? — Take the Autonomous Monorail Transport to the Warehouse to explore and find anything that can help you set up the laser. Heads up, you might have company along the way.  Fire the Laser — Hit the button in the Laser Head Control Room. Watch the show. We're not saying it's the most powerful laser in the 'verse. We're just not saying it isn't. Mine the Asteroid — Navigate into the cracked asteroid and collect your rewards from within: ship-mineable resources of varying rarity. This is why you came.   ▲ Is there anything optional I can do to improve my results?  Yes. Once operational power is restored, you can pursue additional steps to supercharge the laser before firing. How you do this is up to you to find out. More effort in, better results out.   ▲ What's a Sadaryx crystal?  A resource found within the caverns that can be mined and used to craft laser lenses. Useful. Pretty. Definitely worth grabbing.   ▲ Any last tips?  •	Explore properly – There might be components you'll need or loot you'll want along the way.  •	Bring some friends – A group of people with different expertise can help everyone get the most out of each run. •	Do the optional steps – Maybe the simplest route is not always the most rewarding. •	Bring cargo space – There's always something else you'd want to bring home.   ▲ Is there more to do at QV Breaker Stations? At launch, QV Breaker Stations are accessed through the Mining Rights contracts. In the future, these derelict facilities will be home to other activities, bringing more freeform ways to engage.

title: Alpha 4.7 - Welcome to the Rock
summary: Hi everyone,  The Keeger Belt has been quiet for three hundred years, but not forgotten. Abandoned QV Breaker Stations dot the asteroid fields of Nyx, their colossal rock-cracking machinery sitting dormant and untouched. Shubin Interstellar is offering exclusive or shared access rights to anyone willing to go in and wake them back up, and the rare and remarkable resources locked inside make it worth the effort.  Gather your most industrious team and make way to Nyx. A breadth of skills is essential to uncover, claim, and secure the haul: miners, haulers, fighters, and crafters all have a role to play.  Beyond Operation Breaker Stations, Alpha 4.7: Welcome to the Rock brings long-awaited Crafting to the 'verse, letting you fabricate FPS armor and weapons from blueprints and gathered materials. Inventory management also gets a significant overhaul to help you make the most of everything you haul back.  Alongside all of this, RSI reimagines its beloved starter ship with the introduction of the Aurora Mk II, as the Mk I's journey comes to a close and the torch is passed on to light the next chapter. Star Citizen Alpha 4.7: Welcome to the Rock is now available.   Enjoy everything Alpha 4.7 has to offer: Alpha 4.7 "Welcome to the Rock" - Visit the official Alpha 4.7 page to learn more!
